title: సంస్కృత సోపానం · Sanskrit Sopanam
summary: A complete Sanskrit course for Telugu speakers: from the alphabet you already know, through every part of Sanskrit grammar mapped to Telugu grammar, to the Bhagavad Gītā, the Viṣṇu Sahasranāmam and the great stotras.

units.title: ప్రవేశిక · Getting started
units.summary: How the course is laid out, how to study with it, and why a Telugu speaker already knows half of Sanskrit.

lessons.title: ఈ కోర్సు ఎలా వాడాలి · How to use this course
lessons.summary: The staircase (సోపానం) from letters to stotras, what each kind of box means, and a daily routine that makes it stick.

blocks.text: సోపానం — a staircase, one step at a time
This course climbs from what you already know to what you want to read. Every step uses the one below it, so go in order the first time; later, jump around freely.

items: **అక్షరమాల · Script and sounds.** Telugu and Devanagari are sister scripts with the same alphabet order. You will read Devanagari in a day, and learn exactly which Telugu letters Sanskrit does not use (ఎ, ఒ, ఱ…) and which sounds a Telugu speaker must adjust.

**రెండు భాషల వంతెన · The bridge.** How Telugu grammar works (the way Chinnaya Sūri's బాలవ్యాకరణం taught it) set side by side with Sanskrit grammar: genders, cases, verbs and sentences. Then two lessons that list what only Telugu has and what only Sanskrit has.
**మొదటి వాక్యాలు · First sentences.** Everyday spoken Sanskrit: introducing yourself, home, food, time, requests and short dialogues.
**Nouns, pronouns, numbers, verbs, participles.** Every declension class and every tense and mood (లకారం), with full tables, each one tied to a Gītā or Sahasranāmam line where it appears.
**సంధి, సమాసం, తద్ధితం, అవ్యయం.** Joining sounds, compounds, secondary suffixes and indeclinables: the tools that make stotra lines look impossible until you can take them apart.
**వాక్య నిర్మాణం, ఛందస్సు.** Kāraka (who does what to whom), case rules, verse word order (అన్వయం) and metre.
**శ్లోక పఠనం · Readers.** Graded readings from subhāṣitas to the Gītā, the Viṣṇu Sahasranāmam and the stotras, each read the traditional Telugu way: పదచ్ఛేదం → అన్వయం → ప్రతిపదార్థం → తాత్పర్యం.
**జ్ఞాపకం · Memory.** Techniques, cheat sheets and a study plan.

blocks.title: తెలుగులో
text: How the same idea works in Telugu. Start from here: it is the part you already know.

blocks.title: Telugu ↔ Sanskrit
text: A direct comparison, often a trap where Telugu habit gives the wrong Sanskrit.

blocks.title: Memory aid
text: A trick, rhyme, chant or picture to make a rule stick. Every titled memory aid also becomes a flash card.

blocks.title: Pāṇini's sūtra
text: The rule as Pāṇini stated it in the అష్టాధ్యాయీ, with its number. You do not have to memorise sūtras, but they are short and chantable, and many teachers quote them.

blocks.title: Watch out
text: A common mistake.

blocks.title: Note
text: Extra detail you can skip on the first reading.

blocks.text: Worked examples show the Sanskrit in your chosen script with IAST underneath, then the word split (పదచ్ఛేదం), prose order (అన్వయం), word-by-word meaning (ప్రతిపదార్థం), the Telugu and English meaning, and grammar notes. Tap **🔊** to hear it read aloud (by your phone's or Mac's Hindi or Telugu voice: an approximation, not a pandit).

Settings let you show Sanskrit in **తెలుగు లిపి** or **देवनागरी**, with the other script and IAST underneath if you like. Start with Telugu script so nothing slows you down; switch to Devanagari after Unit 1 so that you can read any Sanskrit book. Lessons about the scripts themselves always show both.

items: **Cards.** Every table row, worked example and titled memory aid becomes a flash card. *Learn* shows the whole card; *Test* hides the answer until you tap. Cards you get right come back after 1, 3, 7, 16 and then 35 days; cards you miss come back tomorrow. Choose **Due today** to practise only what needs reviewing.
**Quiz.** Multiple-choice questions for each lesson, with an explanation for every answer. Your best score per lesson is kept.
**Lipi (లిపి).** Type or paste Sanskrit in Telugu script, Devanagari or IAST and see it in the other two. Useful for reading Devanagari books and for typing Sanskrit with a Telugu keyboard.

head: Time
What to do
rows: Cards → *Due today* in Test mode. Never skip this, even on busy days.
One new lesson section. Read it aloud, Sanskrit lines especially.
Copy one table by hand from memory, then check it.
Chant the lesson's verse or paradigm until you can say it without looking.
Take the quizzes of the week's lessons; redo any below 80%.

blocks.title: Say it aloud, write it once, test it tomorrow
text: Sanskrit was memorised by sound for three thousand years. Chanting a table aloud (రామః రామౌ రామాః…) uses the same memory that keeps film songs in your head. Writing it once fixes the spelling. Testing it the next day, before you have forgotten it completely, is what moves it to long-term memory.

quiz.q: In what order should you take the units the first time?
options: In order: script, the bridge, first sentences, then grammar, then readers
Start with the Gītā readers and look up grammar as needed
Any order: the units are independent
quiz.why: Each step builds on the one below it. After one pass you can jump around.

quiz.q: What does the Cards "Due today" option show?
options: Only the cards whose review date has come, based on your earlier answers
quiz.why: Correct answers push a card's next review further out (1, 3, 7, 16, 35 days). Missed cards come back the next day.

quiz.q: Which reading order do the Readers follow, the same order Telugu commentaries use?
quiz.why: Split the sandhi, put the words in prose order, give word meanings, then the overall meaning.

lessons.title: మీకు ఇప్పటికే తెలిసిన సంస్కృతం · The Sanskrit you already know
lessons.summary: Telugu is a Dravidian language, but half its learned vocabulary is Sanskrit. Tatsama and tadbhava words, the Telugu endings that hide Sanskrit stems, and how to recover the stem from the Telugu word.

blocks.text: Telugu and Sanskrit belong to different language families: Telugu is Dravidian (with Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam), Sanskrit is Indo-European (with Greek, Latin, Persian). Their **grammars** are built differently, as Unit 2 shows. But for more than a thousand years Telugu has borrowed Sanskrit words, so a Telugu speaker already knows thousands of Sanskrit stems. Your job is mostly to learn how Sanskrit *inflects* words you already know.

blocks.title: తత్సమం, తద్భవం, దేశ్యం
text: Traditional Telugu grammar sorts words into four kinds. **తత్సమం** (same as that, i.e. Sanskrit) words are Sanskrit stems with a Telugu ending added: రాముడు, వనము, నది. **తద్భవం** (born from that) words were reshaped by Prakrit and Telugu sound changes: అక్కరము from अक्षरम्, బ్రహ్మ → బమ్మ, ఆజ్ఞ → ఆన. **దేశ్యం** words are native Telugu: అమ్మ, ఇల్లు, ఊరు, చెట్టు. **అన్యదేశ్యం** are other borrowings: కుర్చీ, బస్సు.

blocks.text: Telugu endings that hide the Sanskrit word
A tatsama in Telugu is the Sanskrit **stem** plus a Telugu ending. Strip the Telugu ending, then add the Sanskrit one.

blocks.title: -డు is రామః, -స్సు is मनः, -త్తు is जगत्
text: The Telugu ending tells you the Sanskrit class. -డు → masculine అ-stem (రాముడు → रामः). -స్సు → s-stem neuter (మనస్సు → मनः). -త్తు → t-stem (జగత్తు → जगत्). -మంతుడు/-వంతుడు → -मत्/-वत् (బుద్ధిమంతుడు → बुद्धिमान्). Telugu doubled the final consonant and added ఉ because a Telugu word cannot end in a consonant.

blocks.title: The Telugu word is not the Sanskrit nominative
text: You cannot say రాముడు or గురువు in Sanskrit, and మనస్సు is not a Sanskrit form at all (Sanskrit says मनः). Always ask: what is the stem, and which Sanskrit ending does it take? A good habit: when you meet a tatsama in Telugu, say its Sanskrit nominative to yourself.

blocks.text: Some tatsama words changed meaning in Telugu. Reading the Gītā with the Telugu meaning gives the wrong sense.

head: Word
Telugu meaning
Sanskrit meaning
rows: putting near; a statement, a proposal
contentment, being satisfied with what one has
pride, conceit (Gītā 16.4 lists it among demonic traits)

blocks.title: प्रमादः in the Gītā
text: Gītā 14.8 says तमस् binds through प्रमाद, आलस्य, निद्रा: carelessness, laziness, sleep. Not "accidents". When a word looks familiar, check it in a Sanskrit dictionary before trusting the Telugu meaning.

blocks.title: Telugu pronunciation of Sanskrit
text: Telugu speakers pronounce Sanskrit very well compared with most Indian languages: aspirates, ఋ, ష, ణ and the long vowels survive in educated speech. Unit 1 lists the few habits to correct: జ్ఞ said as గ్న, short ఎ/ఒ, ఋ as రు, and dropping the visarga.

items: **Vocabulary is mostly free.** Of the first hundred words in the Gītā, a Telugu speaker recognises most: धर्म, क्षेत्र, पुत्र, युद्ध, आचार्य, सेना, शङ्ख, रथ, धनुस्...

**Grammar is the new part.** Sanskrit inflects nouns in 8 cases × 3 numbers and verbs in 10 tenses/moods × 3 persons × 3 numbers × 2 voices. Telugu agglutinates suffixes instead. Unit 2 shows how the two systems line up.

**Telugu helps with sandhi and compounds.** Telugu has its own sandhis and compounds (సమాసాలు), and literary Telugu uses Sanskrit compounds and sandhis (సవర్ణదీర్ఘ, గుణ, వృద్ధి, యణాదేశ) directly. You learnt them at school.

notes: Every stem is familiar: ధర్మ, క్షేత్ర, కురు, సమవేత. What is new are the endings: -ए (locative "in"), -आः and -अवः (nominative plural).
The first word of the Gītā already teaches the locative ending -ए = Telugu -లో / -అందు.
blocks.te: ధర్మక్షేత్రమైన కురుక్షేత్రంలో యుద్ధం చేయాలనే కోరికతో చేరినవారు…
blocks.en: On the field of dharma, on the field of the Kurus, assembled and eager to fight…

quiz.q: The Telugu word బుద్ధిమంతుడు comes from which Sanskrit stem?
quiz.why: Telugu -మంతుడు = Sanskrit -मत्. The nominative masculine is बुद्धिमान्, like श्रीमान्, हनुमान्.
The stem is मनस्; its nominative/accusative neuter singular is मनः. Telugu doubled the s and added ఉ.
Telugu ప్రమాదం has shifted to "accident"; Sanskrit प्रमाद is "heedlessness".

quiz.q: Which kind of word is ఇల్లు?
quiz.why: ఇల్లు is Dravidian. The Sanskrit word for house is गृहम्, which Telugu also has as గృహము (tatsama).

quiz.q: విష్ణువు is a Telugu form of which Sanskrit nominative?
quiz.why: Telugu adds -వు to u-stems: గురువు (गुरुः), విష్ణువు (विष्णुः), ధేనువు (धेनुः).

units.title: అక్షరమాల · Script and sounds
units.summary: Telugu and Devanagari side by side, letter by letter: vowels, consonants, ం and ః, conjuncts, correct pronunciation, IAST, syllable weight and Pāṇini's sound list (the Māheśvara sūtras).

lessons.title: రెండు లిపులు, ఒకే వర్ణమాల · Two scripts, one alphabet
lessons.summary: Telugu and Devanagari both descend from Brāhmī and list the letters in the same order. Learn the five differences in how they write, and you can read Devanagari in a day.

blocks.text: Both scripts come from the Brāhmī script of Aśoka's inscriptions (3rd century BCE). Telugu-Kannada grew in the south, Nāgarī in the north. The **alphabet** (వర్ణమాల) is the same: vowels first, then consonants grouped by where they are pronounced, from the throat to the lips. Even Unicode encodes them in the same order, which is why this app can turn any Devanagari text into Telugu script exactly.

blocks.title: మీరు ఇప్పటికే నేర్చినది
text: The అ ఆ ఇ ఈ… క ఖ గ ఘ ఙ… order you learnt in school is Pāṇini's order. The గుణింతం (క కా కి కీ…) and ఒత్తులు (క్క, క్ష…) work the same way in Devanagari; only the shapes differ.

head: Feature
తెలుగు
देवनागरी
rows: a straight line (शिरोरेखा) joins the letters of a word: रामः
గుణింతాలు around the letter: కి కీ కు కూ కె కే
मात्रा: कि की कु कू के को. ि is written **before** the letter but said after
half letters side by side or stacked: क्त, स्त, प्र
only ए, ओ (always long in Sanskrit)

blocks.title: ि comes first, is said last
text: In Devanagari the short-i sign ि is written to the left of its consonant: कि = క + ి. Read the consonant first, then the vowel. Every other vowel sign is written where you would expect it.

head: తెలుగు
देवनागरी
IAST
rows: అ ఆ ఇ ఈ ఉ ఊ
अ आ इ ई उ ऊ
a ā i ī u ū

blocks.title: Letters that look alike
text: Several Devanagari letters resemble their Telugu sisters once you add the top line: ग/గ (both have an open curve), ज/జ, ट/ట, ठ/ఠ, ड/డ, प/ప, ल/ల. Others look different and simply have to be learnt: क, ख, घ, ध, भ, म, श, ह.

head: Pair
Difference
rows: ब has a line across the inside; व is an open loop
भ has a notch at top left; म is a closed box
ध has a closed loop on the left and a break in the top line; घ has no loop
ख is one letter with a joined loop; रव is two letters
ष has a slash across the middle
the dot (nukta) is only for Hindi; Sanskrit never uses it
ढ has an extra curl at the bottom
श has a loop at top left and a hook; स a bowl and bar

blocks.title: Learn ten letters a day
text: Day 1: the vowels and their mātrās. Day 2: क-वर्ग and च-वर्ग. Day 3: ट, त, प वर्गs. Day 4: य र ल व श ष स ह and the conjuncts क्ष, ज्ञ, त्र, श्र. Each day, read the names above aloud and use Lipi with Devanagari as the primary script for five minutes.

notes: Read it in Devanagari letter by letter: ॐ (the sacred syllable, written as one sign) · न मो (म + ो) · भ ग व ते (त + े) · वा सु दे वा य.
नमः becomes नमो before भ: a visarga sandhi you will learn in Unit 8.
blocks.te: ఓం నమో భగవతే వాసుదేవాయ — భగవంతుడైన వాసుదేవునికి నమస్కారం.
blocks.en: Om, salutations to the Lord Vāsudeva.

options: ki — the ि sign is written before क but said after it
quiz.why: The short-i mātrā sits on the left of the consonant, but the syllable is क + इ = ki.

quiz.q: Which Telugu vowels have no Sanskrit counterpart?
quiz.why: Sanskrit has only ए and ओ, which are always long. Telugu added short ఎ and ఒ for Dravidian words.

quiz.q: What does the Devanagari शिरोरेखा do?
options: It joins the letters of a word with one top line
quiz.why: The head line runs over every letter of a word; the gaps between words are where it breaks.

quiz.q: How does Devanagari usually write a conjunct like स्त?
options: The first consonant as a half letter beside the second
The second consonant as an ఒత్తు below
quiz.why: Telugu puts the second consonant underneath as an ఒత్తు; Devanagari writes the first as a half-form (स् → स्‍) joined to the next.

options: ब has a line across the inside; व does not
ब has a top line, व does not
quiz.why: Learn this pair early: बालः (boy) vs वालः (tail hair), वनम् (forest) vs बलम् (strength).

lessons.title: అచ్చులు · Vowels (स्वराः)
lessons.summary: The thirteen Sanskrit vowels, their signs in both scripts, short and long, the diphthongs, and the vowels Telugu has but Sanskrit lacks.

blocks.text: Sanskrit measures vowels in **mātrās** (beats). A short vowel (హ్రస్వం, ह्रस्वः) is one mātrā, a long one (దీర్ఘం, दीर्घः) is two, and a prolonged vowel (ప్లుతం, प्लुतः), used in calling out and in Vedic chant, is three. Telugu uses exactly the same terms.

blocks.title: ऊकालोऽज्झ्रस्वदीर्घप्लुतः (1.2.27)
text: A vowel lasting one, two or three times the time of the sound "u" is called hrasva, dīrgha or pluta.

blocks.title: ए and ओ are always long
text: Telugu has short ఎ, ఒ and long ఏ, ఓ. Sanskrit has only the long ones. देव is దేవ, never దెవ; लोक is లోక, never లొక. When you write Sanskrit in Telugu script, always use ే and ో. (Many Telugu books print ె and ొ for Sanskrit; read them as long.)

blocks.text: **Simple vowels** (సమానాక్షరాలు): अ इ उ ऋ ऌ and their long forms. **Diphthongs** (సంధ్యక్షరాలు, सन्ध्यक्षराणि): ए ऐ ओ औ, so called because each was once a blend of two sounds:
This table is the heart of vowel sandhi (Unit 8), and the reason ए and ओ are counted long: they are two vowels fused.

blocks.title: గుణ, వృద్ధి సంధులు
text: Your school Telugu grammar already teaches these as Sanskrit sandhis used in Telugu: గుణసంధి (అ + ఇ = ఏ, అ + ఉ = ఓ, అ + ఋ = అర్) and వృద్ధిసంధి (అ + ఏ = ఐ, అ + ఓ = ఔ). They are exactly Pāṇini's rules.

blocks.text: ऋ is a **vowel**: a syllabic r, sounded as the core of a syllable. Southern traditions, including most Telugu pandits and vedic reciters, say it as a short రు (కృష్ణ ≈ క్రుష్ణ); the north says रि (क्रिष्ण). Both are traditional. What matters is that it stays **short** and counts as **one vowel**: kṛ-ṣṇa is two syllables, and the కృ syllable is light (one mātrā), which matters for metre.

blocks.title: ऋ is the vowel of ऋषि and कृष्ण
text: Remember the vowel through words you say daily: ऋषि (sage), ऋतु (season), कृपा, कृष्ण, हृदय, मृत्यु, पितृ, मातृ. In each, ृ makes the syllable; there is no separate vowel after the r.

blocks.title: ॠ, ऌ, ॡ
text: Long ॠ appears mostly in grammar (pl. पितॄन्, "fathers", acc.). ऌ appears in one common root, क्लृप् (to be fit: कल्पते, क्लृप्त). ॡ is listed by grammarians but occurs in no real word.

blocks.text: What Telugu has that Sanskrit lacks

head: Telugu letter
Why Sanskrit lacks it
rows: Dravidian sound; Sanskrit has only ए
old Telugu half-nasal; Sanskrit uses ँ only in Vedic and in sandhi of म्
old Telugu alveolar r; Sanskrit has one र
old Telugu tsa, dza; Sanskrit च ज are palatal only

head: దేవనాగరి
తెలుగు
rows: क का कि की कु कू कृ कॄ के कै को कौ कं कः
క కా కి కీ కు కూ కృ కౄ కే కై కో కౌ కం కః

మ మా మి మీ ము మూ మృ మే మై మో మౌ

blocks.title: Watch र + ु and र + ू
text: In Devanagari र takes its u-signs on the side, not below: रु (ru), रू (rū). And हृ is ह + ृ (hṛ), as in हृदय.

notes: Find each vowel sign: अ (independent) · ो on ज, त, ण · ि on न · ा on श, ण · ु on प.
ऽ (avagraha) shows that an अ has dropped after ओ: शाश्वतो + अयं → शाश्वतोऽयं. It is not pronounced.
blocks.te: అజః నిత్యః శాశ్వతః అయం పురాణః — ఇతడు పుట్టుకలేనివాడు, నిత్యుడు, శాశ్వతుడు, పురాతనుడు.
blocks.en: Unborn, eternal, everlasting, ancient is this (Self). (Gītā 2.20)

quiz.q: In Sanskrit, how long is ए?
options: Short or long, as in Telugu
quiz.why: Sanskrit has no short e or o. Write and say దేవ, లోక with long vowels.

quiz.q: Which two vowels combine to make ओ?
quiz.why: a + u = o (గుణసంధి): सूर्य + उदय → सूर्योदय.

quiz.q: How many syllables does कृष्ण have?
quiz.why: ऋ is a vowel, so कृ is one syllable. The ṣṇ cluster starts the second.

options: An अ dropped after ए or ओ in sandhi
quiz.why: शाश्वतः + अयम् → शाश्वतोऽयम्. The ऽ is silent.

quiz.q: Which letter is not used in Sanskrit?
quiz.why: ఱ is a Telugu letter. ఋ, ఞ are Sanskrit; ळ is used in Vedic Sanskrit and in South Indian recitation.

lessons.title: హల్లులు · Consonants (व्यञ्जनानि)
lessons.summary: The 25 stops in five वर्गs, the four semivowels, the four sibilants and ह. Where and how each is made, and the grid that makes all of Sanskrit phonetics (and half of sandhi) predictable.

blocks.text: The 25 **sparśa** (touch) consonants form a grid. Rows are the place in the mouth (స్థానం), from the throat outwards; columns are the manner (ప్రయత్నం).

blocks.title: పరుషాలు, సరళాలు, స్థిరాలు
text: Telugu grammar calls columns 1 పరుషాలు (క చ ట త ప) and column 3 సరళాలు (గ జ డ ద బ); the rest are స్థిరాలు. The Telugu గసడదవాదేశ సంధి turns పరుషాలు into సరళాలు (వాడు + కొట్టె → వాడు గొట్టె). Sanskrit has the same idea: column 1 ↔ column 3 in sandhi (वाक् + ईशः → वागीशः).

blocks.title: Say the grid down and across
text: Across: hard, hard-breathy, soft, soft-breathy, nasal (క ఖ గ ఘ ఙ). Down: throat, palate, roof, teeth, lips (క చ ట త ప) — the mouth closing from back to front. Chant కచటతప, గజడదబ, ఙఞణనమ until they are automatic: sandhi rules are stated in these columns.

head: Column
Sanskrit name
Pāṇini's term
Telugu name
rows: हश् (with य र ल व ह)

head: Letter
Place
Type
Note
rows: the consonant form of उ; lips lightly touch upper teeth

blocks.title: य र ल व are इ ऋ ऌ उ in disguise
text: Each semivowel belongs to a vowel: इ↔य, ऋ↔र, ऌ↔ल, उ↔व. That is the యణ్ సంధి you know from Telugu (ఇతి + ఆది → ఇత్యాది, సు + ఆగతం → స్వాగతం): before another vowel, इ becomes य, उ becomes व.

blocks.title: Three s-sounds, three places
text: శ palate (శివ), ష roof (విష్ణు), స teeth (సత్య). Put your tongue where the matching వర్గ is made: श with च, ष with ट, स with त. That is also the order of the sūtra शषसर्.

blocks.text: Every sound, vowel or consonant, has its place. This table, from the Pāṇinīya Śikṣā tradition, explains which vowel goes with which consonants.

head: Place
Vowels
Consonants

च छ ज झ ञ य श
ट ठ ड ढ ण र ष

anusvāra ं, and ङ ञ ण न म also use the nose

blocks.title: अकुहविसर्जनीयानां कण्ठः
text: "a, ku (the क-row), h and visarga: throat." This and the following lines (इचुयशानां तालु, ऋटुरषाणां मूर्धा, लृतुलसानां दन्ताः, उपूपध्मानीयानामोष्ठौ…) are the traditional statement of the table above. Students in Telugu pāṭhaśālās still chant them.

notes: Sort the consonants by place. Throat: ह and the visarga of मत्तः. Palate: य (in सर्वस्य). Roof: र (in सर्व, प्र, वर्त). Teeth: स, त. Lips: प, भ, म. Teeth + lips: व.
Hear the aspirate भ in प्रभवो (soft + breath), and hold the double त of मत्तः a moment longer than a single त.
blocks.te: నేనే అందరికీ మూలం; నా నుండే సర్వం ప్రవర్తిస్తుంది. (గీత 10.8)
blocks.en: I am the origin of all; from me everything proceeds.

quiz.q: Which consonant is both voiced and aspirated (soft + breath)?
quiz.why: Column 4 is soft + breath: घ झ ढ ध भ.

quiz.q: Which sibilant is made at the same place as ट?
quiz.why: ष is मूर्धन्य (retroflex) like the ट-row. श is palatal like च, स dental like त.

quiz.q: य is the consonant partner of which vowel?
quiz.why: इ → य before vowels: इति + आदि → इत्यादि.

quiz.q: Telugu పరుషాలు (క చ ట త ప) are which column of the grid?
quiz.why: పరుషం = hard (aghoṣa, alpaprāṇa). సరళాలు (గ జ డ ద బ) are column 3.
ए combines the places of अ (throat) and इ (palate); ओ combines throat and lips.

lessons.title: అనుస్వారం, విసర్గం · Anusvāra ं and visarga ः
lessons.summary: The two "carried" sounds (अयोगवाह). How ं stands for the nasal of the next consonant, how ः is pronounced with its echo, ँ, ऽ and ॐ.

blocks.text: In Telugu the సున్న (ం) is used for any nasal before a consonant: అంగము, పంచ, కంఠ, అంత, కంప. Sanskrit uses ं in the same way, and **pronounces it as the nasal of the next consonant's వర్గ**:

head: Written
Said as
Example
rows: ं + य र ल व श ष स ह
ं at the end of a word

blocks.title: मोऽनुस्वारः (8.3.23) · अनुस्वारस्य ययि परसवर्णः (8.4.58)
text: A final म् before a consonant becomes ं; and ं before a stop becomes the nasal of that stop's class. So the two spellings शंकर and शङ्कर mean the same pronunciation. Printed Gītās use both.

blocks.title: సున్న = next letter's nasal
text: Look at the letter after ं and use the last letter of its row: క → ఙ, చ → ఞ, ట → ణ, త → న, ప → మ. Only before య ర ల వ శ ష స హ is it a true humming nasal.

blocks.title: Final ं is म्
text: At the end of a line or before a vowel, ं must be said and written as म्: रामम् इति, not रामं इति. In verse, एकं शरणं व्रज is fine (consonant follows), but at a pause it is शरणम्.

blocks.text: The visarga ः is a breath "h" after a vowel. It is very common: it ends most nominative singulars (रामः, हरिः, गुरुः) and many plurals (देवाः). Telugu writes and says it as ః (దుఃఖం, అంతఃపురం).
In recitation, the visarga is followed by a faint echo of the vowel before it:

head: Written
Recited
rows: echo of the i in ai
echo of the u in au

blocks.title: Never drop the visarga
text: Telugu speakers often say రామ for रामः or దుఖం for दुःखम्. In Sanskrit the visarga is grammar: रामः is "Rāma (subject)", राम is "O Rāma!". Say it, even if softly.

blocks.title: Visarga changes in sandhi
text: Before consonants and vowels the visarga often changes: रामः + च → रामश्च, रामः + गच्छति → रामो गच्छति, हरिः + अत्र → हरिरत्र. Unit 8 has every rule. When you see ो, श्, स् or र् at the end of a word in a verse, think "a visarga was here".

head: Sign
Name
Use
rows: a nasalised vowel or semivowel; in Sanskrit mostly Vedic, and in sandhi: तान् + लोकान् → तांल्लोकान्
marks a dropped अ: सोऽहम् (सः + अहम्)
the sacred syllable o-m written as one sign
end of a half-verse or sentence
old visarga variants before क/ख and प/फ, seen in some Vedic books

notes: दुःखेषु: visarga inside a word (दुः). अनुद्विग्नमनाः and विगतस्पृहः end in visarga: recite as …manāhā, …spṛhaha.
In विगतस्पृहः the त before the cluster स्प counts as heavy (గురువు) in metre, while स्पृ itself is light. Lesson 1.8 explains syllable weight.
blocks.te: దుఃఖాలలో కలతపడని మనసు గలవాడు, సుఖాలలో ఆశ లేనివాడు… (గీత 2.56)
blocks.en: One whose mind is not shaken in sorrows, who has no craving among pleasures…

quiz.q: How is the ं in शंकर pronounced?
options: As ङ् (the nasal of the क-row)
quiz.why: Before a क-row consonant, anusvāra takes that row's nasal: शङ्कर.

options: harihi, with a faint echo of i
quiz.why: The visarga echoes the preceding vowel: rāmaha, harihi, guruhu.

quiz.q: Why does the visarga matter in रामः?
options: It marks the subject (nominative); राम alone is the vocative "O Rāma"
It only shows a long vowel
quiz.why: Endings carry grammar in Sanskrit. Dropping ः changes the case.

quiz.q: What does ऽ in सोऽहम् stand for?
quiz.why: सः + अहम् → सो + (अ)हम्. The ऽ marks the missing a.

quiz.q: Before which letters is ं a true humming nasal?
options: य र ल व श ष स ह
quiz.why: Before stops it becomes the class nasal; before semivowels, sibilants and ह it nasalises the vowel: संसार, सिंह.

lessons.title: సంయుక్తాక్షరాలు · Conjuncts (संयुक्ताक्षराणि)
lessons.summary: How Devanagari joins consonants, compared with Telugu ఒత్తులు. The special shapes of र, क्ष, ज्ञ, त्र, श्र, द्य, the common Gītā clusters, and how to read a long cluster.

blocks.text: In Telugu, the second consonant of a cluster goes **below** as an ఒత్తు: క్త, స్త, ప్ర, ద్ధ. In Devanagari, the first consonant usually loses its vertical bar and becomes a **half letter** joined to the next: क्त, स्त, प्य. Letters without a vertical bar (ड, ट, द, ह…) stack instead, or use the virāma.

head: Kind
Devanagari
Telugu
Rule
rows: क्ष, ज्ञ, त्र, श्र, द्य, ह्म, ह्य
క్ష, జ్ఞ, త్ర, శ్ర, ద్య, హ్మ, హ్య

head: Form
Devanagari
Telugu
Example
rows: a small hook on top of the next letter: र्म
धर्म ధర్మ, कर्म కర్మ, सूर्य సూర్య, पूर्ण పూర్ణ

blocks.title: Hook above = ర first; foot stroke = ర second
text: The रेफ hook is drawn on top of the next letter but is **said first**: र्म is rm (धर्म = dharma). The slanted foot ्र is **said second**: प्र is pr. If the hook sits over a vowel sign, it still goes before the whole cluster: सूर्य = sū-rya.

blocks.title: ज्ञ is jña, not gna or gya
text: Telugu speech usually says జ్ఞానం as "gnyānam". The letters are ज् + ञ, and the śikṣā sound is "jña", with the tongue at the palate for both. Regional habits (gnya in the south, gya or dnya in the north) are widespread and accepted in recitation, but never write ग्न or ग्य.

blocks.text: How to read a long cluster

items: Find the vowel: it belongs to the **last** consonant of the cluster.
Read the consonants from left to right (top hook first, foot stroke last).
The syllable break goes **inside** the cluster: the first consonant closes the previous syllable. धर्म = dhar-ma, पुत्र = put-ra, लक्ष्मी = lak-ṣmī.

head: Word
Letters
Syllables
rows: क ृ त् स् न व ि त्
प् र त् य क् ष

blocks.title: Same rule in Telugu prosody
text: In Telugu పద్యం, a short vowel before a conjunct becomes గురువు: in "అమ్మ", అ is guru. Sanskrit metre uses exactly the same rule, because the first consonant of the cluster closes the syllable.

notes: उद्धरेत्: द्ध is stacked; read ud-dha-ret.
आत्मनाऽऽत्मानम्: त्म is a half त joined to म; ऽऽ shows a long आ formed by sandhi (आत्मना + आत्मानम्).
बन्धुः: न्ध is a half न joined to ध. In print you may also see बंधु with anusvāra: same sound.
blocks.te: తనను తానే ఉద్ధరించుకోవాలి; తనను తాను దిగజార్చుకోకూడదు. ఎందుకంటే తనకు తానే స్నేహితుడు, తనకు తానే శత్రువు.
blocks.en: One should save oneself by oneself; one should not degrade oneself. For oneself is indeed one's own friend; oneself is indeed one's own enemy.
blocks.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच

quiz.q: In धर्म, which consonant is pronounced first in the cluster?
options: र — the hook on top is said first
quiz.why: The रेफ hook stands for a र before the consonant it sits on: dhar-ma.
क्ष = kṣa: लक्ष्मी, क्षेत्र, मोक्ष.

quiz.q: Where does the syllable break fall in पुत्र?
quiz.why: The first consonant of a cluster closes the previous syllable, so पु becomes heavy.

quiz.q: In प्र, the foot stroke stands for:
quiz.why: A slanted stroke at the foot is र following the consonant: प्रभु, क्रोध, ग्राम.
The written letters are ज् + ञ. Regional pronunciations vary, but the spelling never changes.

lessons.title: ఉచ్చారణ · Pronunciation for Telugu speakers
lessons.summary: Telugu speakers start with an excellent Sanskrit accent. The ten habits to watch, the sounds that are easy for you and hard for others, and drills from the Gītā and the Sahasranāmam.

blocks.text: Telugu keeps nearly all Sanskrit sounds alive: the aspirates (ఖ ఘ ఛ ఝ ఠ ఢ థ ధ ఫ భ), the retroflex row (ట ఠ డ ఢ ణ), ష, the long vowels and the visarga. Hindi speakers lose ण, ष, ऋ and short final vowels; Tamil speakers lose aspiration and voicing. You start well ahead.

head: Telugu habit
Correct Sanskrit
Example
rows: short ఎ, ఒ for ए, ओ
जगत् is jagat, not జగత్తు; भगवान् not భగవానుడు
final ం said as a nasal vowel
final म् is a full m
short syllabic r (రు is the southern custom)
iast: short ఎ, ఒ for e, o
jagat is jagat, not జగత్తు; bhagavān not భగవానుడు
final m is a full m

blocks.title: Telugu final -ఉ is not Sanskrit
text: Telugu adds ఉ to words ending in a consonant (జగత్తు, మనస్సు, హనుమంతుడు). Sanskrit words can end in a consonant, and that consonant is pronounced without any vowel: जगत् (jagat), मनः (manaḥ), भगवान् (bhagavān), वाक् (vāk). Practise stopping sharply.

blocks.text: Sanskrit doubled consonants are held for twice as long, just as in Telugu అమ్మ, అక్క. Telugu speakers do this naturally; keep doing it in Sanskrit: सत्त्व (sat-tva), उत्तम, चित्त, अद्य (single द), पद्म.

blocks.title: Telugu doubles where Sanskrit does not
text: Telugu often doubles a consonant at a word end or before ఉ: జగత్తు, సత్తు. Sanskrit जगत्, सत् have a single त. And Telugu loans like ప్రత్యేకం keep the Sanskrit doubling as is (प्रत्येकम्).

blocks.text: Classical Sanskrit (the Gītā, stotras) has no word stress to learn. What carries the rhythm is **length**: every long vowel is two beats, every short one is one. Say long vowels long, short ones short, and the verse will scan. (Vedic Sanskrit has a pitch accent marked with svaras: उदात्त, अनुदात्त, स्वरित. That is for veda study, not this course.)

blocks.title: Clap the beats
text: Clap once for each short vowel and twice for each long: रा-म (clap-clap, clap). कृ-ष्ण (clap, clap). In verse, a short vowel before two consonants also gets two claps. If your clapping is even, your pronunciation is good.

blocks.text: Drill: the names in the Sahasranāmam

head: Name
Watch
rows: ट् then क: a closed syllable
हृ (ह + ृ), then ष, then श: three different sounds

notes: विश्वं विष्णुः: श then ष, two different sibilants side by side. Do not let them merge.
भूतकृद् भूतभृद्: the द् is a dead consonant, said without a vowel.
वषट्कारो: the ट् closes the syllable वषट्, making ष heavy for the metre.
blocks.te: విశ్వమే తానైనవాడు; అంతటా వ్యాపించినవాడు; యజ్ఞాలు ఎవరి కోసం చేస్తారో ఆయన; భూత, భవిష్యత్, వర్తమానాలకు ప్రభువు; అందరినీ సృష్టించి, పోషించి, అందరిలో తానే ఉన్నవాడు; సకల జీవులకు ఆత్మ, వారిని పెంచి పోషించేవాడు.
blocks.en: The Universe; the all-pervader; He for whom sacrifice is offered; Lord of past, present and future; creator, sustainer and very being of all; the Self and nourisher of all beings.
blocks.speaker: श्रीवेदव्यास उवाच

notes: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते: say the रेफ clearly (kar-), the ण्य cluster (ṇya), long ā in वा and धि short.
मा फलेषु: फ is p + breath, never English f.
सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि: ङ्ग is ṅg; the avagraha ऽ is silent.
blocks.te: కర్మ చేయడంలో మాత్రమే నీకు అధికారం ఉంది, దాని ఫలాలపై ఎప్పుడూ లేదు. కర్మఫలానికి కారణం నువ్వే అనుకోకు. కర్మ చేయకుండా ఉండటంపై కూడా ఆసక్తి పెట్టుకోకు.
blocks.en: Your right is only to act, not to the results. Do not be the cause of the results of action. Do not have any inclination towards inaction.
blocks.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच

quiz.why: Sanskrit allows final consonants. Telugu జగత్తు adds a doubled t and u.

options: The 2nd and 4th of each वर्ग (ख घ, छ झ, ठ ढ, थ ध, फ भ)
quiz.why: Columns 2 and 4 carry the extra breath (महाप्राण).

quiz.q: In Classical Sanskrit verse, what gives the rhythm?
quiz.why: Classical metres are built from light and heavy syllables. Vedic chant adds pitch.
फ is the aspirated p (column 2 of the प-row).

quiz.q: Which pair should a Telugu speaker keep distinct?
options: श in शिव and ष in विष्णु
क and ख only in Hindi words
ए and ऐ only at the end of a word
quiz.why: श is palatal, ष retroflex. They change meaning: शशः (hare) vs षष्ठः (sixth).

lessons.title: రోమన్ లిపి · IAST transliteration
lessons.summary: The standard way to write Sanskrit in Roman letters, used in dictionaries, grammars and online texts. Learn it once so that you can use Monier-Williams, Apte and every English book on Sanskrit.

blocks.text: Most Sanskrit dictionaries (Monier-Williams, Apte), grammars and online corpora write Sanskrit in IAST (International Alphabet of Sanskrit Transliteration). It is exact: every Devanagari letter has one IAST spelling, and you can type it on any keyboard. The Lipi tool converts IAST to both scripts.

head: తెలుగు
देवनागरी
IAST
Tip
rows: e is always long, no macron needed
c is always చ, never k
ph is p + h, not f
ś acute = palatal, ṣ dot = retroflex

blocks.title: Dot below = tongue curled; bar above = long
text: ṭ ḍ ṇ ṣ ṛ are made with the tongue curled back (మూర్ధన్యం). ā ī ū ṝ are long. ś with an accent is palatal. h after a consonant means "with breath". c is చ — so "cakra" is చక్ర, not కక్ర.

blocks.title: English habits mislead
text: th in IAST is థ (t + breath), not English "th"; ph is ఫ, not "f"; c is చ; and an unmarked a is short. "Krishna", "Shiva", "Vishnu" are popular spellings, not IAST: IAST writes kṛṣṇa, śiva, viṣṇu.

blocks.title: Type IAST quickly
text: In the Lipi tool, type IAST with the special letters, or paste from any book. On a Mac, the "ABC – Extended" keyboard types ā with Option-a then a, ṭ with Option-x then t. On a Pixel, Gboard has Telugu and Sanskrit (Devanagari) keyboards, and long-pressing a, i, u, n, s, t, d on the English keyboard offers most IAST letters.

quiz.why: IAST c is always the palatal च: cakra, candra.

quiz.q: What does a dot below a consonant mean in IAST?
options: Retroflex: tongue curled back (ṭ ḍ ṇ ṣ)
quiz.why: The dot marks the మూర్ధన్య row and ṣ.

quiz.q: How is "kṛṣṇa" written in Telugu script?
quiz.why: ṛ = ృ, ṣ = ష, ṇ = ణ.
h after a consonant is aspiration. ṭh (with dot) is ఠ.
ś = శ (palatal), ṣ = ష (retroflex), s = స (dental).

lessons.title: గురు లఘువులు · Syllables and their weight
lessons.summary: How Sanskrit splits words into syllables, which syllables are light (लघु) and heavy (गुरु), and why this matters for chanting and metre. The rules are the same ones Telugu పద్యం uses.

blocks.text: A syllable is a vowel with the consonants before it. When consonants come between two vowels, the **first** goes with the earlier syllable and the rest with the later one.

blocks.title: ह्रस्वं लघु (1.4.10) · संयोगे गुरु (1.4.11) · दीर्घं च (1.4.12)
text: A short vowel is light. It is heavy if a conjunct follows. A long vowel is heavy.

head: Syllable
Weight
Why
rows: short vowel, single consonant or none after
र in राम, म in राम

blocks.title: Same as Telugu ఛందస్సు
text: Your Telugu grammar taught exactly this: దీర్ఘాక్షరం గురువు, సున్నా, విసర్గ కలిగినవి గురువు, సంయుక్తాక్షరానికి ముందున్నది గురువు, మిగిలినవి లఘువు. Telugu writes గురువు as U and లఘువు as I (or ।). Sanskrit books use ऽ (or —) for guru and । (or ∪) for laghu.

blocks.title: Two beats or one
text: A heavy syllable takes two beats (मात्राs), a light one takes one. Heavy = long vowel, or a short vowel that is "closed" by ं, ः or the first consonant of a cluster.

blocks.text: Look at the pattern: in the eight syllables of an అనుష్టుప్ quarter, syllables 5, 6, 7 decide the shape. Here कु (5) is light, रु (6) heavy, क्षे (7) heavy: ल गु गु, the classic anuṣṭubh ending of the first quarter (Unit 12).

blocks.title: ऋ is short
text: कृ, पृ, हृ are light unless a cluster follows. कृष्ण: कृ is heavy only because ष्ण follows. And a long vowel is heavy even before a single consonant: कृ in कृपा is light, पा heavy.

head: Word
Pattern
rows: गु गु ल (गो long; वि before न्द)
iast: gu gu la (go long; vi before nda)

notes: शुक्लाम्बरधरं: शु (गु, before क्ल), क्ला (गु), म्ब… the syllables are शुक् · लाम् · ब · र · ध · रं — गु गु ल ल ल गु.
Syllables 5–7 of the first quarter (ध रं वि) are ल गु गु — the typical anuṣṭubh pattern.
blocks.te: తెల్లని వస్త్రం ధరించినవాడు, సర్వవ్యాపి, చంద్రుని వంటి వర్ణం కలవాడు, నాలుగు భుజాలు కలవాడు…
blocks.en: Clad in white, all-pervading, moon-coloured, four-armed…

quiz.why: ध is followed by the cluster र्म, which makes it guru.

quiz.q: Is a short vowel followed by anusvāra heavy or light?
quiz.why: ं and ः close the syllable: रं, मः are guru.

quiz.q: How many beats (mātrās) is a heavy syllable?
quiz.why: Light = one mātrā, heavy = two.

quiz.q: What is the weight pattern of केशव?
quiz.why: के has long ए (गु); श and व are short with single consonants after them.

quiz.q: In Telugu prosody, the guru mark is:
options: ऽ only in Sanskrit, nothing in Telugu
quiz.why: Telugu writes గురువు as U and లఘువు as I. Sanskrit books often use ऽ and ।.

lessons.title: మాహేశ్వర సూత్రాలు · Pāṇini's sound list
lessons.summary: The fourteen Śiva sūtras that open Pāṇini's grammar, and the pratyāhāra trick that lets one short word name a whole group of sounds. You need a few of them to read sandhi rules.

blocks.text: Tradition says that at the end of his dance, Śiva (Naṭarāja) sounded his ḍamaru fourteen times, and Pāṇini heard in it the fourteen sūtras that list every Sanskrit sound in a clever order. They are chanted at the start of grammar study:

blocks.title: నృత్తావసానే నటరాజరాజో ననాద ఢక్కాం నవపఞ్చవారమ్
text: "At the end of his dance, the king of dancers sounded his drum nine and five times, to raise up Sanaka and the other sages; these are the Śiva sūtras." The verse continues उद्धर्तुकामः सनकादिसिद्धान् एतद्विमर्शे शिवसूत्रजालम् ॥ — learn it with the sūtras.

blocks.text: Each sūtra lists sounds (with an अ added only for pronunciation) and ends with a **marker consonant** (इत्, shown in brackets) that is not part of the list.

head: Sūtra
Sounds
Marker
rows: kh ph ch ṭh th c ṭ t

blocks.title: Chant them in four breaths
text: అఇఉణ్ ఋఌక్ ఏఓఙ్ ఐఔచ్ (vowels) · హయవరట్ లణ్ (semivowels) · ఞమఙణనమ్ ఝభఞ్ ఘఢధష్ జబగడదశ్ (voiced stops) · ఖఫఛఠథచటతవ్ కపయ్ శషసర్ హల్ (unvoiced and sibilants). Four breaths, fourteen sūtras.

blocks.text: प्रत्याहारः — naming a group with two letters
Take any sound, then a marker: the **pratyāhāra** means "from this sound up to the marker", leaving out the markers in between.

blocks.title: आदिरन्त्येन सहेता (1.1.71)
text: A first sound together with a final marker denotes itself and everything in between.

head: Pratyāhāra
From … to marker
Sounds
Used for
rows: vowels that turn into y v r l (यण्)
every consonant except nasals and य व र ल
खरि च: before unvoiced, become hard
iast: vowels that turn into y v r l (yaṇ)
every consonant except nasals and ya va ra la
khari ca: before unvoiced, become hard

blocks.title: Why ह appears twice
text: ह is listed in sūtra 5 (among the voiced sounds, so it is in हश्) and again in sūtra 14 (so that शल्, the sibilants plus ह, can be named). The ण् marker also appears twice (sūtras 1 and 6); context decides which is meant.

blocks.text: The rule **इको यणचि** (6.1.77) reads: "इक् (i u ṛ ḷ) becomes यण् (y v r l) before अच् (a vowel)". In one breath it gives you four sandhis:

blocks.title: యణాదేశ సంధి
text: Telugu school grammar teaches this very rule as యణాదేశ సంధి: "ఇ ఉ ఋ లకు అసవర్ణములైన అచ్చులు పరమగునపుడు క్రమముగా య వ ర లు ఆదేశమగును". Now you know its Pāṇini form: इको यणचि.

quiz.q: What does the pratyāhāra अच् name?
quiz.why: अ … च् runs from sūtra 1 to the end of sūtra 4: a i u ṛ ḷ e o ai au.
From य in sūtra 5 to the marker ण् of sūtra 6: y v r l.

options: A marker (इत्) that is not one of the sounds
quiz.why: The final consonant of each sūtra marks the end of a group, so that pratyāhāras can be formed.

options: i u ṛ ḷ become y v r l before a vowel
vowels become long before a similar vowel
quiz.why: इक् = i u ṛ ḷ; यण् = y v r l; अचि = before a vowel. Telugu calls it యణాదేశ సంధి.

quiz.q: According to tradition, where did the sūtras come from?
options: Śiva's ḍamaru at the end of his dance
quiz.why: नृत्तावसाने नटराजराजो ननाद ढक्कां नवपञ्चवारम्: fourteen strokes of the drum.

units.title: రెండు భాషల వంతెన · The Telugu–Sanskrit bridge
units.summary: How Telugu grammar works, the way Bālavyākaraṇam teaches it, mapped point by point onto Sanskrit grammar: words, gender and number, cases, verbs and sentences. Then what only Telugu has, and what only Sanskrit has.

lessons.title: పెద్ద చిత్రం · The big picture
lessons.summary: Telugu glues suffixes on one after another; Sanskrit fuses meaning into a single ending. Parts of speech in both traditions, and the three facts that explain most differences.

blocks.text: Telugu is **agglutinative** (అతుకు): each suffix does one job, and suffixes are stacked in a fixed order. Sanskrit is **fusional** (కలయిక): one ending carries several meanings at once.

blocks.title: Telugu builds, Sanskrit chooses
text: In Telugu you **build** a word: stem + plural + case. In Sanskrit you **choose** the right ending from a table: रामेभ्यः is one block. That is why Sanskrit needs tables (శబ్దాలు, ధాతురూపాలు) and Telugu needs rules for joining.

head: Telugu (బాలవ్యాకరణం)
Sanskrit (Pāṇini, Yāska)
What it covers
rows: pronouns: अस्मद्, युष्मद्, तद्, यद्, किम्, सर्व…
indeclinables: च, न, इति, एव, हि, तु
verb prefixes: प्र, परा, सम्, अनु…
iast: pronouns: asmad, yuṣmad, tad, yad, kim, sarva…
indeclinables: ca, na, iti, eva, hi, tu
verb prefixes: pra, parā, sam, anu…

blocks.title: सुप्तिङन्तं पदम् (1.4.14)
text: "A word (पद) is what ends in a सुप् or a तिङ् ending." Every Sanskrit word in a sentence is either a declined noun (सुबन्त) or a conjugated verb (तिङन्त), or an indeclinable (which grammar treats as having a zero ending). There are no bare stems in a sentence.

blocks.title: Telugu too has two kinds of endings
text: Telugu attaches విభక్తి ప్రత్యయాలు to nouns (డు, ని, చేత, కొఱకు…) and క్రియా ప్రత్యయాలు to verbs (-ను, -వు, -ఆడు…). The difference is that Telugu suffixes stack (రాముల-కు, పోతున్న-ాడు) while Sanskrit endings are single blocks.

blocks.text: Three facts that explain most differences

items: **Word order is free in Sanskrit.** Because the ending shows the role, रामः रावणं हन्ति, रावणं रामः हन्ति and हन्ति रामः रावणम् all mean "Rāma kills Rāvaṇa". Telugu is fixed: subject–object–verb (రాముడు రావణుని చంపెను), with the verb at the end. In prose, Sanskrit also prefers subject–object–verb, so Telugu order is a good default.

**Sanskrit marks gender, number and case on adjectives too.** Telugu adjectives do not change: మంచి బాలుడు, మంచి బాలిక, మంచి పిల్లలు. Sanskrit adjectives agree: सुन्दरः बालः, सुन्दरी बाला, सुन्दराः बालाः.
**Sanskrit verbs do not show gender; Telugu verbs do.** వాడు వచ్చాడు, ఆమె వచ్చింది — the Telugu verb changes with the gender of the subject. Sanskrit says सः आगच्छत्, सा आगच्छत्: the same verb.

blocks.title: One verse, two word orders
text: Gītā 2.47 says कर्मणि एव अधिकारः ते: "in action alone (is) right your". Telugu prose order is నీకు కర్మయందే అధికారం. The Sanskrit is free to put कर्मणि first for emphasis, because -इ already says "in".

head: Telugu grammar
Sanskrit grammar
rows: సంజ్ఞా పరిచ్ఛేదం: terms (అచ్చులు, హల్లులు, ద్రుతం, కళ…)
संज्ञा sūtras: technical terms (वृद्धि, गुण, इत्, पद…)
తత్సమ పరిచ్ఛేదం: how Sanskrit words enter Telugu
iast: saṃjñā sūtras: technical terms (vṛddhi, guṇa, it, pada…)

blocks.title: The two great grammars
text: Pāṇini's Aṣṭādhyāyī (c. 5th century BCE, about 4,000 sūtras) describes all of Sanskrit. Telugu's first grammar, Nannaya's Āndhra Śabda Cintāmaṇi, was written in Sanskrit on Pāṇini's model; Chinnaya Sūri's Bālavyākaraṇam (1858) is the school grammar most Telugu speakers know. That shared heritage is why Telugu grammar terms map so well onto Sanskrit ones.

sa: रामः रावणं हन्ति । रावणं रामः हन्ति । हन्ति रामः रावणम् ।
notes: The endings -ः (subject) and -म् (object) do the work that word order does in English. Swap them, रामं रावणः हन्ति, and the meaning reverses.
blocks.te: రాముడు రావణుని చంపుతున్నాడు (మూడు వాక్యాలకూ ఒకే అర్థం).
blocks.en: Rāma kills Rāvaṇa (all three sentences mean the same).
iast: rāmaḥ rāvaṇaṃ hanti | rāvaṇaṃ rāmaḥ hanti | hanti rāmaḥ rāvaṇam |

quiz.q: Why can Sanskrit words be put in almost any order?
options: The endings show each word's role (case)
Sanskrit has no grammar for order
quiz.why: रामः is the subject wherever it stands; रावणम् is the object.

options: Telugu verbs show the subject's gender; Sanskrit verbs do not
Sanskrit verbs show gender; Telugu verbs do not
quiz.why: వాడు వచ్చాడు / ఆమె వచ్చింది vs सः आगच्छत् / सा आगच्छत्.

quiz.q: What is a पद according to Pāṇini?
options: A word ending in a सुप् (noun) or तिङ् (verb) ending
quiz.why: सुप्तिङन्तं पदम् (1.4.14). Bare stems don't appear in sentences.

options: Agree with their noun in gender, number and case
quiz.why: सुन्दरः बालः, सुन्दरी बाला, सुन्दरम् फलम्.

options: Telugu stacks separate suffixes; Sanskrit picks one fused ending from a table
quiz.why: బాలురకు = బాలు-ర-కు (plural + dative); बालेभ्यः is a single ending.

lessons.title: లింగం, వచనం · Gender and number
lessons.summary: Telugu sorts nouns by meaning (మహత్, అమహత్); Sanskrit gives every noun a grammatical gender, often arbitrarily. Telugu has two numbers; Sanskrit has three, including the dual.

blocks.text: Telugu grammar divides nouns by what they refer to:

head: Telugu class
Covers
Verb form
Example
rows: women (in the singular they go with అమహత్ verbs)

blocks.text: The gender follows **meaning**: a stone is అమహత్, a man is మహత్.

Sanskrit has **पुंलिङ्ग** (masculine), **स्त्रीलिङ्ग** (feminine) and **नपुंसकलिङ्ग** (neuter). People usually take their natural gender, but things and ideas are assigned a gender by the word, not the meaning:

blocks.title: Gender comes with the word, not the thing
text: The same thing can have words of different genders: "wife" is दाराः (m. pl.), कलत्रम् (n.) and भार्या (f.); "body" is देहः (m.), शरीरम् (n.) and तनुः (f.). Learn every noun with its nominative ending, which usually tells you the gender: -ः often masc., -आ/-ई fem., -म् neuter.

blocks.title: Three questions for a new noun
text: (1) What is the stem? (2) What is the gender? (3) What is the nominative singular? Learn धर्मः (m.), not "dharma"; ज्ञानम् (n.), not "jñāna"; मतिः (f.), not "mati". The nominative + gender tells you which table to use.

blocks.title: Telugu కర్మము, Sanskrit कर्म
text: Telugu -ము hides the gender. Sanskrit -अन् nouns are neuter when they mean an action or thing (कर्म, जन्म, नाम, धाम) and masculine when they mean a person (आत्मा, राजा, ब्रह्मा — but ब्रह्म n. "the Absolute").

blocks.text: Telugu has ఏకవచనం and బహువచనం. Sanskrit has **एकवचनम्**, **द्विवचनम्** (exactly two) and **बहुवचनम्** (three or more).

blocks.title: Two is special
text: Whenever there are exactly two — two eyes, two hands, Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa — Sanskrit uses the dual, and the verb is dual too: रामलक्ष्मणौ वनं गच्छतः. The dual endings are few (three per noun class, three per verb tense), so learn them as a set.

blocks.title: Respect plural, and the plural of dignity
text: Telugu uses the plural for respect: మీరు, వారు, గురువుగారు వచ్చారు. Sanskrit can do this too (भवन्तः, "your honours"), but usually uses भवान् (singular "your honour") with a third-person verb: भवान् कुत्र गच्छति? Some nouns are always plural: दाराः (wife), प्राणाः (life breath), अप्सरसः, सिकताः (sand).

notes: श्वेतैर्हयैर्युक्ते: श्वेतैः हयैः युक्ते "yoked with white horses": instrumental plural (the horses), then locative singular (the chariot).
माधवः पाण्डवश्चैव "Mādhava (Kṛṣṇa) and the Pāṇḍava (Arjuna)": two subjects…
…so the verb is dual: प्रदध्मतुः "the two blew", and the object is dual: दिव्यौ शङ्खौ "two divine conches".
blocks.te: అప్పుడు తెల్లని గుర్రాలు కట్టిన గొప్ప రథంపై ఉన్న మాధవుడు (శ్రీకృష్ణుడు), పాండు కుమారుడు (అర్జునుడు) తమ దివ్య శంఖాలను ఊదారు.
blocks.en: Then Mādhava and the son of Pāṇḍu, standing on a great chariot yoked to white horses, blew their divine conches.
blocks.speaker: सञ्जय उवाच

sa: बालकः पठति । बालकौ पठतः । बालकाः पठन्ति ।
notes: Both the noun and the verb change with number. Telugu changes only the noun for two vs. many.
blocks.te: బాలుడు చదువుతున్నాడు. ఇద్దరు బాలురు చదువుతున్నారు. బాలురు చదువుతున్నారు.
blocks.en: The boy reads. The two boys read. The boys read.
iast: bālakaḥ paṭhati | bālakau paṭhataḥ | bālakāḥ paṭhanti |

quiz.q: What is the gender of वृक्षः (tree)?
options: Neuter, because it is a thing
quiz.why: Sanskrit gender belongs to the word. वृक्षः ends in -ः like रामः.

quiz.q: How many numbers does Sanskrit have?
quiz.why: एकवचनम्, द्विवचनम्, बहुवचनम्.
Two people: dual noun (-औ) and dual verb (-तः).

quiz.q: What gender is a noun ending in -ति like भक्तिः, शक्तिः?
quiz.why: Action nouns in -ति are feminine: मतिः, गतिः, भक्तिः.

quiz.q: Which Sanskrit word for "wife" is always masculine plural?
quiz.why: दाराः is masculine and always plural; भार्या is feminine, कलत्रम् neuter. Gender is a property of the word.

lessons.title: విభక్తులు · Cases: Telugu ప్రత్యయాలు and Sanskrit सुप्
lessons.summary: Both languages count eight cases with the same names, because Telugu grammarians took the names from Sanskrit. The Bālavyākaraṇam suffixes set against the Sanskrit endings, and the places where the two disagree.

blocks.text: You learnt this verse-like list at school. Each line is one విభక్తి and its Telugu suffixes (ప్రత్యయాలు):

blocks.title: డుముపులు ప్రథమ…
text: Chant the Telugu list as you learnt it — డుముపులు ప్రథమ, నిన్ నున్ లన్ గూర్చి గుఱించి ద్వితీయ, చేతన్ చేన్ తోడన్ తోన్ తృతీయ, కొఱకున్ కై చతుర్థి, వలనన్ కంటెన్ పట్టి పంచమి, కిన్ కున్ యొక్క లోన్ లోపలన్ షష్ఠి, అందున్ నన్ సప్తమి, ఓ ఓరి ఓయి ఓసి సంబోధన — and after each line say the Sanskrit form: रामः, रामम्, रामेण, रामाय, रामात्, रामस्य, रामे, हे राम.

blocks.title: Why the names are the same
text: Telugu grammarians (Nannaya, then Chinnaya Sūri) described Telugu with the Sanskrit framework, so they kept the Sanskrit names and numbers: ప్రథమా = प्रथमा ("first"), ద్వితీయా = द्वितीया ("second")… The cases **mean** mostly the same things, which is a great help.

blocks.text: Sanskrit has 7 cases + vocative, each in 3 numbers: 21 endings, called **सुप्** after Pāṇini's list.

blocks.title: स्वौजसमौट्छष्टाभ्याम्भिस्ङेभ्याम्भ्यस्ङसिभ्याम्भ्यस्ङसोसाम्ङ्योस्सुप् (4.1.2)
text: The 21 basic endings in one breath: सु औ जस् · अम् औट् शस् · टा भ्याम् भिस् · ङे भ्याम् भ्यस् · ङसि भ्याम् भ्यस् · ङस् ओस् आम् · ङि ओस् सुप्. Each noun class reshapes them (राम + टा → रामेण), but the skeleton is the same for all nouns. The name सुप् comes from the first (सु) and last (सुप्) endings.

blocks.text: The meanings line up well, but not perfectly. These mismatches cause most beginners' mistakes:

head: Meaning
Telugu
Sanskrit
Example
rows: నాకు పుస్తకం ఉంది → मम पुस्तकम् अस्ति
నాకు పండు ఇష్టం → मह्यं फलं रोचते
iast: నాకు పుస్తకం ఉంది → mama pustakam asti
నాకు పండు ఇష్టం → mahyaṃ phalaṃ rocate

blocks.title: The -కి trap
text: Telugu uses -కి / -కు for "to a place", "to a person", "I have", "I like" and "I know". Sanskrit uses four different cases. Ask what -కి really means each time: going somewhere → accusative (వనం గచ్ఛతి); giving to someone → dative (రామాయ దదాతి); having → genitive (మమ అస్తి).

blocks.title: షష్ఠీ for "among"
text: Gītā 10.21 आदित्यानाम् अहं विष्णुः "among the Ādityas I am Viṣṇu" uses the genitive plural, Telugu ఆదిత్యులలో. Sanskrit uses षष्ठी or सप्तमी for "the best among" (निर्धारण): नराणां च नराधिपम् "and among men, the king" (10.27).

blocks.text: What Telugu does that Sanskrit doesn't: postpositions

Telugu adds many meanings with separate words after the noun: మీద (on), కింద (under), దగ్గర (near), వెనుక (behind), ముందు (before), నుండి (from), వరకు (until), కోసం (for). Sanskrit uses either a case alone or an indeclinable with a case:

notes: परित्राणाय, विनाशाय, धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय: three datives of purpose (చతుర్థీ, Telugu -కొఱకు, -కై).
साधूनाम्, दुष्कृताम्: genitive plurals: "of the good", "of the evildoers".
युगे युगे: locative of time, repeated: "in age after age", Telugu యుగయుగమునందు.
blocks.te: సజ్జనులను రక్షించడానికి, దుష్టులను నాశనం చేయడానికి, ధర్మాన్ని స్థాపించడానికి నేను ప్రతి యుగంలోనూ అవతరిస్తాను.
blocks.en: For the protection of the pious, the destruction of the evil-doers, and the establishment of virtue, I manifest myself in every age.
blocks.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच

sa: मम पुस्तकम् अस्ति । अहं ग्रामं गच्छामि । मह्यं फलं रोचते ।
notes: Three Telugu "నాకు / -కి" sentences, three different Sanskrit cases: genitive, accusative, dative.
blocks.te: నాకు పుస్తకం ఉంది. నేను ఊరికి వెళ్తున్నాను. నాకు పండు ఇష్టం.
blocks.en: I have a book. I am going to the village. I like fruit.
iast: mama pustakam asti | ahaṃ grāmaṃ gacchāmi | mahyaṃ phalaṃ rocate |

quiz.why: Possession uses the genitive (षष्ठी): मम "of me".

quiz.q: "రాముడు అడవికి వెళ్ళెను" — what case is "అడవికి" in Sanskrit?
quiz.why: The goal of a motion verb is accusative: वनं गच्छति.

quiz.q: Which Telugu suffixes belong to the తృతీయా?
quiz.why: తృతీయా = instrument and agent: रामेण "by / with Rāma".

quiz.q: "రాముని కంటే గొప్పవాడు" uses which Sanskrit case for रामः?
quiz.why: Comparison "than" takes the ablative: रामात् श्रेष्ठः.

quiz.q: How many सुप् endings does Pāṇini list?
quiz.why: The vocative uses the nominative endings with small changes, so the list has 21.

quiz.q: In गृहस्य पुरतः ("in front of the house"), गृहस्य is in which case?
quiz.why: Most "place" words (पुरतः, पृष्ठतः, उपरि, अधः, समीपे) take the genitive.

lessons.title: క్రియలు · Verbs: Telugu forms and Sanskrit लकारs
lessons.summary: Every Telugu verb form you know (చేసెను, చేయుచున్నాడు, చేయును, చేయుము, చేసి, చేయుచు, చేయుటకు, చేసిన…) and its Sanskrit equivalent: a lakāra (tense or mood) or a kṛdanta (participle). Persons and numbers, which even share their names.

blocks.text: పురుషలు — the same names, the same order
Both traditions count persons from the **third**: the one spoken about comes first. The names are identical.

blocks.title: "First person" means opposite things
text: In English grammar "first person" is I. In both Telugu and Sanskrit grammar, ప్రథమ పురుష / प्रथमपुरुषः is **he/she/it**, and ఉత్తమ పురుష / उत्तमपुरुषः is **I**. Sanskrit verb tables list he → you → I.

blocks.title: ప్రథమ మధ్యమ ఉత్తమ = తి సి మి
text: The present tense of every Sanskrit verb runs -ति, -सि, -मि in the singular: भवति (he is), भवसि (you are), भवामि (I am). Read the table he–you–I and the endings almost spell "ti si mi".

blocks.text: Telugu verb forms and their Sanskrit counterparts
Chinnaya Sūri lists the Telugu verb forms by meaning (అర్థకాలు). Here is each one with its Sanskrit match, using కృ / చేయు (do).

blocks.title: క్త్వార్థకం, శత్రర్థకం, తుమున్నర్థకం
text: These Telugu grammar terms **are** Sanskrit suffix names: క్త్వా (→ कृत्वा), శతృ (→ कुर्वन्), తుమున్ (→ कर्तुम्). Chinnaya Sūri named the Telugu forms after the Sanskrit suffixes with the same meaning. So you already know the Sanskrit terms: you just need the forms.

blocks.text: The ten लकारs at a glance
Sanskrit has ten tense/mood sets, all named with ल + a vowel. Unit 6 teaches each one.

blocks.title: लट् वर्तमाने लेट् वेदे
text: The traditional verse: लट् वर्तमाने लेट् वेदे भूते लुङ् लङ् लिटस्तथा । विध्याशिषोस्तु लिङ्लोटौ लुट् लृट् लृङ् च भविष्यति ॥ "लट् for the present, लेट् in the Veda; लुङ्, लङ्, लिट् for the past; लिङ् and लोट् for command and blessing; लुट्, लृट्, लृङ् for the future." Chant it until it's automatic.

blocks.text: Two things Sanskrit verbs have that Telugu verbs don't

items: **Two "voices" of endings: परस्मैपद and आत्मनेपद.** भवति, करोति use one set; वर्तते, लभते, मन्यते use another. Some verbs take both (करोति / कुरुते): traditionally the आत्मनेपद is "for oneself". Telugu has nothing like it.
**Dual endings:** भवतः (two are), भवथः (you two are), भवावः (we two are).

blocks.text: And one thing Telugu verbs have that Sanskrit verbs don't: **gender**. వచ్చాడు / వచ్చింది / వచ్చారు — Sanskrit says आगच्छत् for all three singulars. (Sanskrit participles like गतः / गता / गतम् do show gender, which is why spoken Sanskrit often uses them.)

notes: मा भूः "do not be" is the classical prohibitive: मा + aorist (लुङ्) without the augment अ: अभूः → भूः. Telugu నిషేధార్థకం: కాకుము.
अस्तु "let it be" is लोट् (command / wish), 3rd person: Telugu ఉండుగాక.
ते is the short form of तव / तुभ्यम् "your / to you". Telugu నీకు.
blocks.split: कर्मणि एव अधिकारः ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुः भूः मा ते सङ्गः अस्तु अकर्मणि ॥
blocks.te: కర్మ చేయడంలో మాత్రమే నీకు అధికారం ఉంది, దాని ఫలాలపై ఎప్పుడూ లేదు. కర్మఫలానికి కారణం నువ్వే అనుకోకు. కర్మ చేయకుండా ఉండటంపై కూడా ఆసక్తి పెట్టుకోకు.
blocks.en: Your right is only to act, not to the results. Do not be the cause of the results of action. Do not have any inclination towards inaction.
blocks.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
blocks.split_iast: karmaṇi eva adhikāraḥ te mā phaleṣu kadācana | mā karmaphalahetuḥ bhūḥ mā te saṅgaḥ astu akarmaṇi ||

quiz.q: In Sanskrit grammar, प्रथमपुरुषः refers to:
options: he / she / it (third person in English terms)
quiz.why: As in Telugu ప్రథమ పురుష, the person spoken about comes first: सः भवति.
क्त्वा = "having done". కర్తుమ్ is తుమున్ (to do), కుర్వన్ is శతృ (doing).

quiz.q: Which lakāra is used for commands?
quiz.why: लोट्: कुरु (do!), भवतु (let it be). लट् is present, लृट् future.
The prohibitive is मा + aorist without augment. न + imperative is avoided in classical Sanskrit.

quiz.q: Which feature do Telugu verbs have that Sanskrit verbs lack?
quiz.why: వచ్చాడు / వచ్చింది vs आगच्छत् for both.

quiz.q: What is the Sanskrit form for "to do" (Telugu చేయుటకు)?
quiz.why: तुमुन् = infinitive of purpose: Telugu తుమున్నర్థకం.

lessons.title: వాక్యాలు · Sentences side by side
lessons.summary: How a Telugu sentence is built and how the same thought is built in Sanskrit: "is" sentences, agreement, questions, "and", "not", quoting with అని / इति, relative clauses, and the passive.

blocks.text: 1. "X is Y" — no verb needed in either
Telugu says రాముడు మంచివాడు without "is". Sanskrit can do the same: रामः साधुः. The verb अस्ति is optional in the present.

blocks.title: The predicate agrees
text: In Sanskrit the predicate noun or adjective takes the same case (nominative) and, if it is an adjective, the same gender and number: सीता साध्वी, फलं मधुरम्, वृक्षाः उन्नताः. Telugu adjectives never change: మంచి.

blocks.text: Telugu adds -ఆ to the end of a word or uses a question word: నువ్వు వచ్చావా? ఎవరు వచ్చారు? Sanskrit puts **किम्** or **अपि** at the start for a yes/no question, or uses a question word (क-words):

head: Telugu
Sanskrit
rows: किं त्वम् आगमिष्यसि? / अपि त्वम् आगमिष्यसि?
iast: kiṃ tvam āgamiṣyasi? / api tvam āgamiṣyasi?

blocks.title: క-words ask, య-words relate, త-words point
text: కః (who?), యః (who, the one that), సః (he). కదా (when?), యదా (when, as in "when X…"), తదా (then). కుత్ర (where?), యత్ర (where…), తత్ర (there). One pattern, dozens of words. Gītā 18.78: यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णः … तत्र श्रीः "where Kṛṣṇa is … there is fortune".

blocks.text: Telugu adds -ఊ (-ఉ) to each word: రాముడూ సీతా వచ్చారు. Sanskrit puts **च** after the last word (or after each): रामः सीता च आगच्छताम्; रामश्च सीता च.

blocks.title: च never starts a sentence
text: Telugu ఇంకా, మరియు can begin a sentence. Sanskrit च, वा, अपि, एव, तु, हि are **enclitic**: they always come after the word they attach to. सर्वधर्मान् परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज: एकम् "alone" emphasises माम्.

blocks.text: Telugu builds negative verb forms: చేయను, చేయలేదు, రాడు. Sanskrit simply puts **न** before the verb (or the word negated): न करोमि, न अकरोत्, न आगच्छति.

blocks.title: Gītā 2.20
text: न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचित् "it is not born, nor does it ever die": one न covers both verbs. Telugu needs two negative verbs: పుట్టదు, చావదు.

blocks.text: Telugu ends a quotation or thought with **అని**: "నేను వస్తాను" అని చెప్పాడు. Sanskrit uses **इति** in exactly the same place:

blocks.title: అని = इति, exactly
text: This is one of the closest matches between the two languages. Telugu అనగా, అనే, అని all have Sanskrit इति behind them. Gītā 3.27: कर्ता अहम् इति मन्यते "he thinks 'I am the doer'" = నేను కర్తను అని తలంచును.

blocks.text: Telugu uses an **adjectival participle** before the noun: నేను చదివిన పుస్తకం. Sanskrit has two ways:
The यद्–तद् pair is everywhere in the Gītā: यः … सः, या … सा, यत् … तत्, यदा … तदा, यत्र … तत्र.

notes: यद्यत् … तत्तत्: "whatever … that very thing": the relative pronoun doubled for "whatever".
सः यत् प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकः तत् अनुवर्तते: "what standard he sets, that the world follows": a यत् … तत् pair.
Telugu builds the same thought with a participle: శ్రేష్ఠుడు ఏది ఆచరిస్తాడో, దానినే ఇతరులూ ఆచరిస్తారు — Telugu too uses ఏది…అదే, a borrowed relative pattern.
blocks.te: శ్రేష్ఠుడు ఏది చేస్తాడో ఇతరులు కూడా అదే చేస్తారు. అతను దేనిని ప్రమాణంగా నిలబెడతాడో లోకం దానినే అనుసరిస్తుంది.
blocks.en: Whatever a superior person does, another person does the same! Whatever they uphold as authority, an ordinary person follows that.
blocks.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच

blocks.text: Telugu rarely uses the passive (చేయబడెను sounds bookish). Sanskrit uses it all the time, especially with past participles: "by Rāma Rāvaṇa (was) killed" is the normal way to say "Rāma killed Rāvaṇa".

blocks.title: Passive = agent in తృతీయా, object in ప్రథమా
text: Swap the roles: the doer goes into the instrumental (రామునిచేత → रामेण), the thing done becomes the subject (रावणः), and the verb or participle agrees with it (हतः). Telugu: రామునిచేత రావణుడు చంపబడెను.

sa: अहं गीतां पठामि इति माता जानाति । किं त्वम् अपि पठसि ?
notes: इति closes the quoted thought, as అని does.
"అమ్మకు తెలుసు" becomes माता जानाति: the knower is the subject in Sanskrit.
blocks.te: నేను గీత చదువుతున్నానని అమ్మకు తెలుసు. నువ్వు కూడా చదువుతున్నావా?
blocks.en: Mother knows that I am reading the Gītā. Are you reading it too?
iast: ahaṃ gītāṃ paṭhāmi iti mātā jānāti | kiṃ tvam api paṭhasi ?

quiz.q: Where does च go in "Rāma and Sītā"?
options: After the last word (or after each): रामः सीता च
Between them: रामः च सीता only
quiz.why: च is enclitic and follows the word it joins. रामश्च सीता च is also correct.
Both close a quotation or thought: "…" इति = "…" అని.

quiz.q: How is a yes/no question usually marked in Sanskrit?
options: किम् or अपि at the start (or just intonation)
-आ at the end, as in Telugu
quiz.why: किं त्वम् आगमिष्यसि? Telugu uses వస్తావా with -ఆ.

quiz.q: "నేను చదివిన పుస్తకం" with a participle in Sanskrit:
quiz.why: The past participle पठितम् agrees with पुस्तकम्, and the reader goes in the instrumental: मया.

quiz.q: In the passive रामेण रावणः हतः, who did the killing?
quiz.why: The agent of a passive is in the instrumental; the patient (Rāvaṇa) is nominative.

lessons.title: తెలుగులో మాత్రమే · What Telugu has and Sanskrit lacks
lessons.summary: Features of Telugu grammar with no Sanskrit counterpart: gender in verbs, inclusive "we", negative conjugation, ద్రుతం, human and non-human numbers, Telugu-only sandhis and more. Knowing them stops you carrying them into Sanskrit.

head: Telugu feature
Example
In Sanskrit instead
rows: Feminine singular takes the neuter verb
सीता आगच्छत्, gender not on the verb
మనం (you and I) / మేము (we, not you)
द्वौ बालकौ / द्वे धेनू: by gender, not humanness
Words never end in a consonant
जगत्, मनः end in consonant / visarga
the pronoun भवान्, words like श्री, पूज्य
nominative subject: अहं बुभुक्षितः, अहं जानामि
Short ఎ, ఒ; ఱ; ౘ, ౙ
iast: sītā āgacchat, gender not on the verb
dvau bālakau / dve dhenū: by gender, not humanness
jagat, manaḥ end in consonant / visarga
the pronoun bhavān, words like śrī, pūjya
nominative subject: ahaṃ bubhukṣitaḥ, ahaṃ jānāmi

blocks.title: Telugu -కొను and Sanskrit आत्मनेपद
text: One near-match: Telugu -కొను adds "for oneself" (చేసుకొను, చదువుకొను). Sanskrit expresses "for oneself" with आत्मनेपद endings: यजते "he sacrifices for himself" vs यजति "he sacrifices (for another, as a priest)". Unit 6 explains when this distinction still matters.

blocks.title: Don't carry Telugu negatives into Sanskrit
text: Telugu has a separate negative form for each person (చేయను, చేయవు, చేయడు). In Sanskrit, just put न before the ordinary verb: न करोमि, न करोषि, न करोति. And "don't!" is मा: मा शुचः "don't grieve" (Gītā 18.66).

blocks.text: Telugu has its own sandhis (తెలుగు సంధులు) alongside the Sanskrit ones it borrows. None of these exists in Sanskrit; the Sanskrit sandhis are in Unit 8.

head: Telugu sandhi
Rule
Example
rows: అ at a word end may drop before a vowel
ఇ of ఏమి, మఱి, అది… may drop
final ఉ drops before a vowel (always)
య is inserted between vowels when no sandhi
in a repeated word, the vowel may join
ఔర + ఔర → ఔరౌర, ఏమి + ఏమి → ఏమేమి
కుఱు, చిఱు, కడు, నడు, నిడు + vowel: ఱ, డ → ట్ట
క చ ట త ప → గ స డ ద వ after ప్రథమ / ద్రుతం
ఆ, ఈ, ఏ + consonant: consonant doubles, vowel shortens
ప్రాత, లేత… lose their final syllable

blocks.title: Sanskrit sandhis used in Telugu
text: Literary Telugu also uses the Sanskrit sandhis for Sanskrit words: సవర్ణదీర్ఘ (రామ + అయనం → రామాయణం), గుణ (మహా + ఇంద్ర → మహేంద్ర), వృద్ధి, యణాదేశ, జశ్త్వ, శ్చుత్వ, అనునాసిక, విసర్గ. Your school grammar called these సంస్కృత సంధులు. They are Pāṇini's rules and you will meet them all in Unit 8.

blocks.text: Many Telugu words end in a "flowing" న్ (ద్రుతం) that appears before vowels and disappears or changes elsewhere: పూచెను + పువ్వులు → పూచెఁ బువ్వులు, పూచెం బువ్వులు, పూచె పువ్వులు. Words with it are ద్రుతప్రకృతికాలు; others are కళలు. Sanskrit has nothing like this. Its final न् and म् follow regular sandhi.

Telugu has human numbers (ఒకడు, ఇద్దరు, ముగ్గురు, నలుగురు) and non-human ones (ఒకటి, రెండు, మూడు, నాలుగు). Sanskrit numbers instead agree in **gender** with the noun: एकः बालः, एका बाला, एकं फलम्; द्वौ बालौ, द्वे बाले, द्वे फले; त्रयः बालाः, तिस्रः बालाः, त्रीणि फलानि.

notes: Sanskrit does not distinguish inclusive and exclusive "we". It distinguishes "we two" from "we (three or more)".
blocks.te: మేము / మనము వెళ్తున్నాము. మేమిద్దరం / మనమిద్దరం వెళ్తున్నాము.
blocks.en: We are going. We two are going.

quiz.q: How does Sanskrit say both మనం and మేము?
quiz.why: Sanskrit has no inclusive/exclusive distinction; it has a dual instead.
Put न before the positive verb. There are no negative conjugations.

quiz.q: Which Telugu sandhi turns క చ ట త ప into గ స డ ద వ?
quiz.why: వాడు + కొట్టె → వాడు గొట్టె. Sanskrit has a similar voicing rule (जश्त्व), but stated differently.

quiz.q: Why does Telugu say జగత్తు where Sanskrit says जगत्?
options: Telugu words cannot end in a consonant, so it doubles and adds ఉ
quiz.why: Sanskrit allows final consonants: जगत्, वाक्, मरुत्.

quiz.q: In Sanskrit, numbers agree with their noun in:
quiz.why: द्वौ बालकौ, द्वे बालिके, द्वे फले: masculine, feminine, neuter forms of "two".

lessons.title: సంస్కృతంలో మాత్రమే · What Sanskrit has and Telugu lacks
lessons.summary: The new machinery you must learn: the dual, three arbitrary genders, agreeing adjectives, many noun classes, ten lakāras, two sets of verb endings, ten verb classes, prefixes, derived verbs, obligatory sandhi, huge compounds and absolute constructions. A map of the rest of this course.

blocks.text: The list, with where each is taught

Telugu has

हे राम, हे हरे, हे गुरो
causative कारयति, desiderative जिज्ञासते, intensive, denominative
गतः, गतवान्, गच्छन्, गमिष्यन्, गन्तव्य, गमनीय
