blocks.title: Telugu names work the same way
text: Telugu given names are Sahasranāma names: శ్రీనివాస్, పద్మనాభం, హృషీకేశ్, మధుసూదన్, జనార్దన్, పురుషోత్తం, గోవింద్, కేశవ్. Each of them is a compound or a kṛt noun. When you meet a friend's name in the stotram, analyse it: that is the easiest way to remember a type.

blocks.text: The names run into each other with sandhi. Split them with the method of lesson 8.6, and use these signs:

items: Every name ends in a case ending, usually -ः, -म्, -आ or -ई. A र्, ो or ऽ in the middle of a line usually marks the end of a name: स्थाणुर्भूतादिः = स्थाणुः भूतादिः.
च and एव च fill the metre; they are not names.
A few splits are disputed, and commentators count the names differently. In verse 12, समात्माऽसम्मितः can be read as समात्मा + असम्मितः or समात्मा + सम्मितः; Śaṅkara explains both.
Some names appear more than once (विष्णुः in verses 1 and 70). The commentators give each occurrence a different meaning, so nothing is counted twice.

sa: पूतात्मा परमात्मा च मुक्तानां परमा गतिः।
अव्ययः पुरुषः साक्षी क्षेत्रज्ञोऽक्षर एव च॥
notes: मुक्तानां परमा गतिः is one name made of three words: a genitive plural, a feminine adjective and a feminine noun. Names do not have to be single words.
पूतात्मा and परमात्मा are an-stems (आत्मन्), nominative -आ (lesson 4.9).
क्षेत्रज्ञः + अक्षरः → क्षेत्रज्ञोऽक्षरः, and अक्षरः + एव → अक्षर एव (lesson 8.5).
blocks.split: पूतात्मा परमात्मा च मुक्तानां परमा गतिः । अव्ययः पुरुषः साक्षी क्षेत्रज्ञः अक्षरः एव च ॥
blocks.te: పరిశుద్ధమైన ఆత్మ; పరమాత్మ; ముక్తులకు చివరి గమ్యం; నాశనం లేనివాడు; పురుషుడు; సాక్షి; క్షేత్రాన్ని (శరీరాన్ని) తెలిసినవాడు; క్షయం లేనివాడు.
blocks.en: The pure Self; the Supreme Self; highest goal of the liberated; the imperishable; the Purusha; the witness; knower of the field; and the indestructible.
blocks.speaker: श्रीवेदव्यास उवाच
iast: pūtātmā paramātmā ca muktānāṃ paramā gatiḥ|
avyayaḥ puruṣaḥ sākṣī kṣetrajño'kṣara eva ca||
blocks.split_iast: pūtātmā paramātmā ca muktānāṃ paramā gatiḥ | avyayaḥ puruṣaḥ sākṣī kṣetrajñaḥ akṣaraḥ eva ca ||

notes: योगविदां नेता: a genitive plural (योगविद्, consonant stem) with an agent noun in -तृ (नेता, from नी).
प्रधानपुरुषेश्वरः: प्रधानस्य पुरुषस्य च ईश्वरः, a dvandva inside a tatpuruṣa. नारसिंहवपुः: a bahuvrīhi on the -उस् stem वपुस्; नारसिंह is a taddhita from नरसिंह.
पुरुषोत्तमः: पुरुषेषु उत्तमः (7th case of the group) or, with Gītā 15.18, the one beyond both the perishable and the imperishable.
blocks.split: योगः योगविदां नेता प्रधानपुरुषेश्वरः । नारसिंहवपुः श्रीमान् केशवः पुरुषोत्तमः ॥
blocks.te: యోగం ద్వారా పొందదగినవాడు; యోగులకు నాయకుడు; ప్రకృతికి, పురుషునికి ప్రభువు; నరసింహ రూపం ధరించినవాడు; శ్రీమంతుడు; కేశవుడు; పురుషోత్తముడు.
blocks.en: Attainable through yoga; leader of yogis; Lord of Prakriti and Purusha; of the man-lion form; the glorious Keshava; the Supreme Person.
blocks.speaker: श्रीवेदव्यास उवाच
blocks.split_iast: yogaḥ yogavidāṃ netā pradhānapuruṣeśvaraḥ | nārasiṃhavapuḥ śrīmān keśavaḥ puruṣottamaḥ ||

notes: अप्रमेयः: न प्रमेयः, the gerundive of प्र + मा "measure" with the negative (lesson 7.4): "not to be measured".
पद्मनाभः: पद्मं नाभौ यस्य सः. नाभि becomes -नाभ at the end of a bahuvrīhi. विश्वकर्मा is a bahuvrīhi on the an-stem कर्मन्.
स्थविष्ठः is the irregular superlative of स्थूल "gross, large" (lesson 10.2). त्वष्टा is a -तृ agent noun.
blocks.split: अप्रमेयः हृषीकेशः पद्मनाभः अमरप्रभुः । विश्वकर्मा मनुः त्वष्टा स्थविष्ठः स्थविरः ध्रुवः ॥
blocks.te: కొలవలేనివాడు; ఇంద్రియాలకు ప్రభువు; నాభిలో పద్మం ఉన్నవాడు; దేవతలకు ప్రభువు; విశ్వాన్ని నిర్మించేవాడు; ఆలోచించేవాడు; రూపాలను తీర్చిదిద్దేవాడు; అతి విశాలుడు; అతి ప్రాచీనుడు; స్థిరుడు, శాశ్వతుడు.
blocks.en: Immeasurable; Lord of the senses; lotus-naveled; Lord of the immortals; architect of the universe; the thinker; the shaper; the vast; the ancient; the fixed and eternal.
blocks.speaker: श्रीवेदव्यास उवाच
blocks.split_iast: aprameyaḥ hṛṣīkeśaḥ padmanābhaḥ amaraprabhuḥ | viśvakarmā manuḥ tvaṣṭā sthaviṣṭhaḥ sthaviraḥ dhruvaḥ ||

sa: ईशानः प्राणदः प्राणो ज्येष्ठः श्रेष्ठः प्रजापतिः।
notes: ईशानः: the ātmanepada participle of ईश् "rule" in -आन (lesson 7.2), used as a name.
ज्येष्ठः and श्रेष्ठः are the irregular superlatives of वृद्ध "old" and प्रशस्य "praiseworthy" (lesson 10.2).
माधवः: मा (= लक्ष्मी) + धव "husband", "husband of Lakṣmī"; it is also explained as a taddhita from मधु. मधुसूदनः: मधुं सूदयति इति, a kṛt noun in -अन (lesson 7.5).
blocks.split: ईशानः प्राणदः प्राणः ज्येष्ठः श्रेष्ठः प्रजापतिः । हिरण्यगर्भः भूगर्भः माधवः मधुसूदनः ॥
blocks.te: అందరినీ నియంత్రించేవాడు; ప్రాణాన్ని ఇచ్చేవాడు; ప్రాణమే తానైనవాడు; అందరికంటే పెద్దవాడు; అత్యంత స్తుతించదగినవాడు; ప్రజలకు ప్రభువు; హిరణ్యగర్భుడు; భూమిని ధరించినవాడు; లక్ష్మీపతి (మాధవుడు); మధు రాక్షసుని సంహరించినవాడు.
blocks.en: The controller; giver of life; the life-breath; the eldest; the most praiseworthy; Lord of creatures; the golden-wombed; holder of the earth; consort of Lakshmi; slayer of the demon Madhu.
blocks.speaker: श्रीवेदव्यास उवाच
iast: īśānaḥ prāṇadaḥ prāṇo jyeṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ prajāpatiḥ|
blocks.split_iast: īśānaḥ prāṇadaḥ prāṇaḥ jyeṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ prajāpatiḥ | hiraṇyagarbhaḥ bhūgarbhaḥ mādhavaḥ madhusūdanaḥ ||

sa: ईश्वरो विक्रमी धन्वी मेधावी विक्रमः क्रमः।
notes: Four possessives: विक्रमी, धन्वी (-इन्), मेधावी (-विन्), आत्मवान् (-वत्). They all mean "having …" (lesson 4.8).
अनुत्तमः: न विद्यते उत्तमः यस्मात् सः, "he than whom none is higher", a negative bahuvrīhi.
दुराधर्षः: दुर् + आ + धृष् with the suffix खल् "hard to …", like दुर्लभ (Gītā 7.19).
blocks.split: ईश्वरः विक्रमी धन्वी मेधावी विक्रमः क्रमः । अनुत्तमः दुराधर्षः कृतज्ञः कृतिः आत्मवान् ॥
blocks.te: సర్వశక్తిమంతుడు; పరాక్రమశాలి; విల్లు ధరించినవాడు; గొప్ప బుద్ధిమంతుడు; అడుగులు వేసి లోకాలను కొలిచినవాడు; అంతటా వ్యాపించినవాడు; సాటిలేనివాడు; ఎవరూ ఎదిరించలేనివాడు; చేసినదంతా తెలిసినవాడు; కర్మయే తానైనవాడు; ఆత్మవంతుడు.
blocks.en: The omnipotent; the valiant; the wielder of the bow; supremely intelligent; the strider; all-pervading; unsurpassed; unassailable; knower of all deeds; the very act; and self-possessed.
blocks.speaker: श्रीवेदव्यास उवाच
iast: īśvaro vikramī dhanvī medhāvī vikramaḥ kramaḥ|
blocks.split_iast: īśvaraḥ vikramī dhanvī medhāvī vikramaḥ kramaḥ | anuttamaḥ durādharṣaḥ kṛtajñaḥ kṛtiḥ ātmavān ||

notes: The श्री verse: nine names built on one word with nine different endings. A complete drill of upapadas (श्रीदः, श्रीधरः, श्रीकरः), tatpuruṣas (श्रीशः, श्रीनिवासः, श्रीनिधिः), a kṛt noun (श्रीविभावनः) and a possessive (श्रीमान्).
श्रीमान् + लोक → श्रीमाँल्लोक: न् before ल becomes a nasalised ल्ल (lesson 8.4).
श्रेयः is a neuter -अस् noun used as a name: "the highest good".
blocks.split: श्रीदः श्रीशः श्रीनिवासः श्रीनिधिः श्रीविभावनः । श्रीधरः श्रीकरः श्रेयः श्रीमान् लोकत्रयाश्रयः ॥
blocks.te: సంపదను ఇచ్చేవాడు; లక్ష్మీపతి; లక్ష్మికి నివాసం; శ్రీకి నిధి; భాగ్యాలను పంచేవాడు; లక్ష్మిని ధరించేవాడు; సంపదను సృష్టించేవాడు; పరమ శ్రేయస్సు; శ్రీమంతుడు; మూడు లోకాలకు ఆశ్రయం.
blocks.en: Giver of prosperity; Lord of Lakshmi; abode of Lakshmi; treasury of glory; distributor of fortunes; bearer of Lakshmi; maker of prosperity; the supreme good; the glorious; refuge of the three worlds.
blocks.speaker: श्रीवेदव्यास उवाच
blocks.split_iast: śrīdaḥ śrīśaḥ śrīnivāsaḥ śrīnidhiḥ śrīvibhāvanaḥ | śrīdharaḥ śrīkaraḥ śreyaḥ śrīmān lokatrayāśrayaḥ ||

notes: The स्वस्ति verse: one word with -द, -कृत्, -भुक् and -दक्षिण.
स्वस्तिभुक्: the root भुज् ends in -क् at the end of a word (lesson 8.3). In the archana it is restored: स्वस्तिभुजे नमः.
सनातनतमः: the superlative -तम on सनातन "eternal": "most ancient of all" (lesson 10.2).
blocks.split: सनात् सनातनतमः कपिलः कपिः अव्ययः । स्वस्तिदः स्वस्तिकृत् स्वस्ति स्वस्तिभुक् स्वस्तिदक्षिणः ॥
blocks.te: సనాతనుడు; అత్యంత సనాతనుడు; పింగళ వర్ణ ముని (కపిలుడు); సూర్యుడు; క్షయం లేనివాడు; స్వస్తిని ఇచ్చేవాడు; మేలు చేసేవాడు; స్వస్తియే తానైనవాడు; స్వస్తిని అనుభవించేవాడు; శుభాన్ని ప్రసాదించేవాడు.
blocks.en: The ancient; the most eternal; the tawny sage (Kapila); the sun; the imperishable; giver of well-being; doer of good; well-being itself; enjoyer of well-being; who bestows auspiciousness.
blocks.speaker: श्रीवेदव्यास उवाच
blocks.split_iast: sanāt sanātanatamaḥ kapilaḥ kapiḥ avyayaḥ | svastidaḥ svastikṛt svasti svastibhuk svastidakṣiṇaḥ ||

notes: The यज्ञ verse: five upapadas with bare roots (-भृत्, -कृत्, -भुक्, -अन्तकृत्) and one with -अद (अन्नादः = अन्नम् अत्ति इति).

Final-consonant sandhi in a row: यज्ञभृत् + यज्ञ → यज्ञभृद्यज्ञ (त् → द् before य); यज्ञभुक् + यज्ञ → यज्ञभुग्यज्ञ (क् → ग्). Printed texts often keep a space after the changed consonant: यज्ञभृद् यज्ञकृद् (lesson 8.3).
यज्ञगुह्यम् and अन्नम् are neuter names; their archana datives are यज्ञगुह्याय and अन्नाय.
blocks.split: यज्ञभृत् यज्ञकृत् यज्ञी यज्ञभुक् यज्ञसाधनः । यज्ञान्तकृत् यज्ञगुह्यम् अन्नम् अन्नादः एव च ॥
blocks.te: యజ్ఞాన్ని నిలిపేవాడు; యజ్ఞాన్ని చేసేవాడు; యజ్ఞాన్ని అనుభవించేవాడు; హవిస్సును స్వీకరించేవాడు; యజ్ఞానికి సాధనం; యజ్ఞాన్ని పూర్తి చేసేవాడు; యజ్ఞ రహస్యం; అన్నం, అన్నం తినేవాడు రెండూ తానే.
blocks.en: Upholder of the sacrifice; performer of the sacrifice; the enjoyer of the sacrifice; consumer of the offering; means of the sacrifice; who completes the sacrifice; the secret of the sacrifice; the food and the eater of food.
blocks.speaker: श्रीवेदव्यास उवाच
blocks.split_iast: yajñabhṛt yajñakṛt yajñī yajñabhuk yajñasādhanaḥ | yajñāntakṛt yajñaguhyam annam annādaḥ eva ca ||

notes: The weapons verse. Five ways to say "holding": -भृत् (upapada), -इन् (नन्दकी, चक्री), bahuvrīhi with -धन्वन् and -पाणि, and -धर (upapada).
शार्ङ्गधन्वा: धनुस् becomes -धन्वन् at the end of a bahuvrīhi (धनुषश्च, Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.4.132), so its nominative is -धन्वा.
शङ्खभृत् + नन्दकी → शङ्खभृन्नन्दकी (त् before a nasal becomes न्, lesson 8.4). अक्षोभ्यः is a negative gerundive.
blocks.split: शङ्खभृत् नन्दकी चक्री शार्ङ्गधन्वा गदाधरः । रथाङ्गपाणिः अक्षोभ्यः सर्वप्रहरणायुधः ॥
blocks.te: శంఖం (పాంచజన్యం) ధరించినవాడు; నందకమనే ఖడ్గం ధరించినవాడు; చక్రధారి; శార్ఙ్గమనే విల్లు గలవాడు; గద (కౌమోదకి) ధరించినవాడు; రథచక్రం చేతిలో గలవాడు; కదిలించలేనివాడు; అన్ని ఆయుధాలు ధరించినవాడు.
blocks.en: Bearer of the conch (Panchajanya); wielder of the sword Nandaka; holder of the discus; of the bow Sharnga; bearer of the mace (Kaumodaki); who holds the wheel; the unshakable; armed with all weapons.
blocks.speaker: श्रीवेदव्यास उवाच
blocks.split_iast: śaṅkhabhṛt nandakī cakrī śārṅgadhanvā gadādharaḥ | rathāṅgapāṇiḥ akṣobhyaḥ sarvapraharaṇāyudhaḥ ||

blocks.text: The last verse: the only verb

sa: वनमाली गदी शार्ङ्गी शङ्खी चक्री च नन्दकी।
notes: Six -इन् possessives in one line (lesson 4.8). All are nominative singular in -ई.
अभिरक्षतु is the first and only finite verb of the stotram: a 3rd singular imperative of blessing (lesson 6.6). After a thousand names, one prayer.
वासुदेवः is a taddhita "son of Vasudeva" (lesson 10.1). नारायणः: नराणाम् अयनम्, with the न → ण rule (lesson 6.10).
blocks.split: वनमाली गदी शार्ङ्गी शङ्खी चक्री च नन्दकी । श्रीमान् नारायणः विष्णुः वासुदेवः अभिरक्षतु ॥
blocks.anvaya: वनमाली गदी शार्ङ्गी शङ्खी चक्री नन्दकी च श्रीमान् नारायणः विष्णुः वासुदेवः (अस्मान्) अभिरक्षतु ॥
blocks.te: వనమాల ధరించినవాడు, గద, శార్ఙ్గ విల్లు, శంఖం, చక్రం, నందక ఖడ్గం ధరించినవాడు అయిన శ్రీమన్నారాయణుడు — విష్ణువు, వాసుదేవుడు — మమ్మల్ని ఎల్లప్పుడూ రక్షించాలి.
blocks.en: May the glorious Narayana — Vishnu, Vasudeva — who wears the forest-garland and bears the mace, the Sharnga bow, the conch, the discus and the sword Nandaka, ever protect us.
blocks.speaker: श्रीवेदव्यास उवाच
iast: vanamālī gadī śārṅgī śaṅkhī cakrī ca nandakī|
blocks.split_iast: vanamālī gadī śārṅgī śaṅkhī cakrī ca nandakī | śrīmān nārāyaṇaḥ viṣṇuḥ vāsudevaḥ abhirakṣatu ||
blocks.anvaya_iast: vanamālī gadī śārṅgī śaṅkhī cakrī nandakī ca śrīmān nārāyaṇaḥ viṣṇuḥ vāsudevaḥ (asmān) abhirakṣatu ||

blocks.text: For archana (worship with flowers), each name is put in the 4th case and framed with ॐ … नमः. The dative ending depends on the stem, and a few names surprise you:

blocks.title: Don't just add -आय
text: Beginners write विष्णाय or आत्माय. Find the stem first (lessons 4.2–4.10), then take its dative. The stems that most often catch people: -अन् (आत्मने), -इन् (साक्षिणे), -तृ (त्वष्ट्रे) and the pronoun विश्व (विश्वस्मै).

options: negative + gerundive of प्र + मा: "not to be measured"
quiz.why: -य gerundive with अ-.

quiz.q: How many finite verbs does the whole stotram (verses 1–108) have?
quiz.why: The stotram is a list of names.

quiz.q: The archana form of विश्वम् is:
quiz.why: विश्व declines like the pronoun सर्व.

options: धनुस् becomes -धन्वन् at the end of a bahuvrīhi
quiz.why: धनुषश्च.
न् + ल → ँल्ल.
The root is भुज्; -क् is only the word-final form.

quiz.q: Which of these is a possessive in -इन्?
quiz.why: चक्रम् अस्य अस्ति इति चक्री.

lessons.title: ఫలశ్రుతి · Viṣṇu Sahasranāmam III: the closing verses
lessons.summary: The phala-śruti that follows the names, and the closing prayers. A study in the optative of result (whoever would hear … would gain), the passive optative मुच्येत, the -अर्थी pattern, the neuter plural for mixed subjects, a verse in vaṃśastha, the three meanings of an -ए ending in श्रीराम राम रामेति, and the passive imperative क्षम्यताम्.

blocks.text: The phala-śruti promises results. Its grammar is almost always the same: यः + optative ("whoever would do X"), then the optative again for the result ("would gain Y"). Telugu says "ఎవరు … చదువుతారో, వారు … పొందుతారు".

notes: Three optatives: शृणुयात् (श्रु, class 5), परिकीर्तयेत् (class 10), प्राप्नुयात् (प्र + आप्, class 5): lesson 6.6.
अमुत्र "there (in the next world)" and इह "here" are place adverbs; -त्र is the suffix of अत्र, तत्र, यत्र, सर्वत्र (lesson 10.3).
Sandhi: यः + इदम् → य इदम् (lesson 8.5); शृणुयात् + नित्यम् → शृणुयान्नित्यम् (त् before a nasal becomes न्, lesson 8.4); सः + अमुत्र → सोऽमुत्र.
blocks.split: यः इदं शृणुयात् नित्यं यः च अपि परिकीर्तयेत् । न अशुभं प्राप्नुयात् किञ्चित् सः अमुत्र इह च मानवः ॥
blocks.anvaya: यः मानवः इदं नित्यं शृणुयात्, यः च अपि परिकीर्तयेत्, सः अमुत्र इह च किञ्चित् अशुभं न प्राप्नुयात् ॥
blocks.te: దీనిని రోజూ వినేవారికి, జపించేవారికి — ఇక్కడ గానీ, పరలోకంలో గానీ — ఏ అశుభమూ కలగదు.
blocks.en: Whoever listens to this daily, and whoever recites it, meets with nothing inauspicious — here or hereafter.
blocks.speaker: श्रीभीष्म उवाच
blocks.split_iast: yaḥ idaṃ śṛṇuyāt nityaṃ yaḥ ca api parikīrtayet | na aśubhaṃ prāpnuyāt kiñcit saḥ amutra iha ca mānavaḥ ||
blocks.anvaya_iast: yaḥ mānavaḥ idaṃ nityaṃ śṛṇuyāt, yaḥ ca api parikīrtayet, saḥ amutra iha ca kiñcit aśubhaṃ na prāpnuyāt ||

notes: स्यात् and भवेत् are the optatives of अस् and भू: both mean "would be, becomes". The verse alternates them for variety.
स्यात् + शूद्रः → स्याच्छूद्रः: त् + श becomes च्छ (lesson 8.3).
वेदान्तगः: वेदान्तं गच्छति इति, an upapada with -ग. धनसमृद्धः: धनेन समृद्धः, a tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa. विजयी is a possessive in -इन्.
blocks.split: वेदान्तगः ब्राह्मणः स्यात् क्षत्रियः विजयी भवेत् । वैश्यः धनसमृद्धः स्यात् शूद्रः सुखम् अवाप्नुयात् ॥
blocks.te: విద్య కోరేవాడు వేదాంత జ్ఞానాన్ని పొందుతాడు; క్షత్రియుడు విజయం సాధిస్తాడు; వ్యాపారి ధనవంతుడవుతాడు; శ్రామికుడు సుఖాన్ని పొందుతాడు.
blocks.en: A seeker of knowledge attains Vedānta; a warrior becomes victorious; a merchant prospers; a worker obtains happiness.
blocks.speaker: श्रीभीष्म उवाच
blocks.split_iast: vedāntagaḥ brāhmaṇaḥ syāt kṣatriyaḥ vijayī bhavet | vaiśyaḥ dhanasamṛddhaḥ syāt śūdraḥ sukham avāpnuyāt ||

notes: -अर्थी "one who seeks" is a possessive in -इन् on अर्थ "aim": धर्मः अर्थः यस्य, धर्मार्थी "whose aim is dharma". The pattern is X-अर्थी X-म् आप्नुयात्.
Three verbs from the same root आप्: आप्नुयात्, प्राप्नुयात् (प्र-), अवाप्नुयात् (अव-). The prefixes change the meaning only slightly here (lesson 6.10).
प्रजाः is the accusative plural of the ā-stem प्रजा (lesson 4.4); it looks like the nominative.
blocks.split: धर्मार्थी प्राप्नुयात् धर्मम् अर्थार्थी च अर्थम् आप्नुयात् । कामान् अवाप्नुयात् कामी प्रजार्थी च आप्नुयात् प्रजाः ॥
blocks.te: ధర్మం, ధనం, సుఖాలు, సంతానం — ఏది కోరితే అది పొందుతారు.
blocks.en: One who seeks dharma, wealth, enjoyments, or progeny obtains them.
blocks.speaker: श्रीभीष्म उवाच
blocks.split_iast: dharmārthī prāpnuyāt dharmam arthārthī ca artham āpnuyāt | kāmān avāpnuyāt kāmī prajārthī ca āpnuyāt prajāḥ ||

notes: Four ablatives of release (lesson 11.1): रोगात्, बन्धनात्, भयात्, and आपदः, the ablative of the feminine consonant stem आपद् (it looks like a nominative plural).
मुच्यते is the passive present; मुच्येत is the passive optative (lesson 6.8): the passive stem मुच्य- + the ātmanepada optative ending -एत.
बद्धः, भीतः, आपन्नः are past participles used as nouns: "the bound, the frightened, the one in distress" (lesson 7.1). रोगार्तः = रोगेण आर्तः.
मुच्येत + आपन्नः → मुच्येतापन्नः; आपन्नः + आपदः → आपन्न आपदः (lesson 8.5).
blocks.split: रोगार्तः मुच्यते रोगात् बद्धः मुच्येत बन्धनात् । भयात् मुच्येत भीतः तु मुच्येत आपन्नः आपदः ॥
blocks.te: రోగి రోగం నుండి, బంధించబడినవాడు బంధం నుండి, భయపడినవాడు భయం నుండి, ఆపదలో ఉన్నవాడు ఆపద నుండి విముక్తులవుతారు.
blocks.en: The sick are freed from illness, the bound from bondage, the frightened from fear, and the afflicted from calamity.
blocks.speaker: श्रीभीष्म उवाच
blocks.split_iast: rogārtaḥ mucyate rogāt baddhaḥ mucyeta bandhanāt | bhayāt mucyeta bhītaḥ tu mucyeta āpannaḥ āpadaḥ ||

blocks.title: The release verse
text: Four sufferers, four ablatives, one root: रोगार्तः–रोगात्, बद्धः–बन्धनात्, भीतः–भयात्, आपन्नः–आपदः. Each sufferer is named from the same root as his trouble. Recite it when you revise the ablative.

blocks.text: The one whose refuge is Vāsudeva

words: అన్ని పాపాల నుండి శుద్ధమైన ఆత్మ గలవాడై
notes: Three bahuvrīhis describing मर्त्यः (lesson 9.4): वासुदेवः आश्रयः यस्य सः; वासुदेवः परायणं यस्य सः; सर्वेभ्यः पापेभ्यः विशुद्धः आत्मा यस्य सः.
ब्रह्म here is the accusative of the neuter ब्रह्मन्, the object of याति "goes to". Neuter nominative and accusative are the same.
मर्त्य "mortal" is formed with the suffix -य from मृ "die".
blocks.split: वासुदेवाश्रयः मर्त्यः वासुदेवपरायणः । सर्वपापविशुद्धात्मा याति ब्रह्म सनातनम् ॥
blocks.te: వాసుదేవుని ఆశ్రయించి, ఆయనకు అంకితమైన మనిషి అన్ని పాపాల నుండి శుద్ధుడై, శాశ్వతమైన బ్రహ్మాన్ని పొందుతాడు.
blocks.en: The mortal who takes refuge in Vāsudeva and is devoted to Him, purified of all sin, attains the eternal Brahman.
blocks.speaker: श्रीभीष्म उवाच
blocks.split_iast: vāsudevāśrayaḥ martyaḥ vāsudevaparāyaṇaḥ | sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā yāti brahma sanātanam ||

notes: द्यौः is the nominative of the irregular feminine दिव् "sky" (lesson 4.10). सचन्द्रार्कनक्षत्रा agrees with it: feminine. स- means "together with" (सह) and makes a bahuvrīhi.
The subjects are feminine (द्यौः, दिशः, भूः), neuter (खम्) and masculine (महोदधिः). A shared adjective for subjects of different genders is put in the neuter plural: विधृतानि.
विधृतानि is a past participle in a passive with the instrumental वीर्येण (lesson 6.8).
blocks.split: द्यौः सचन्द्रार्कनक्षत्रा खं दिशः भूः महोदधिः । वासुदेवस्य वीर्येण विधृतानि महात्मनः ॥
blocks.te: చంద్రుడు, సూర్యుడు, నక్షత్రాలతో కూడిన స్వర్గం, ఆకాశం, దిక్కులు, భూమి, మహా సముద్రం — ఇవన్నీ మహాత్ముడైన వాసుదేవుని శక్తితోనే నిలిచి ఉన్నాయి.
blocks.en: Heaven with moon, sun, and stars, the sky, the directions, the earth, and the great ocean — all are upheld by the power of the great Vāsudeva.
blocks.speaker: श्रीभीष्म उवाच
blocks.split_iast: dyauḥ sacandrārkanakṣatrā khaṃ diśaḥ bhūḥ mahodadhiḥ | vāsudevasya vīryeṇa vidhṛtāni mahātmanaḥ ||

words: తామర రేకుల వంటి విశాల నేత్రాలు గలవాడా
notes: Four masculine vocatives in -अ: the bare stem (lesson 4.2).
त्राता is an agent noun in -तृ (त्रै "protect"). Its object is in the 6th case, भक्तानाम्, as with every kṛt noun (कर्तृकर्मणोः कृति; compare Gītā 16.21).
भव is the imperative of भू: "become (the protector)".
blocks.split: पद्मपत्रविशालाक्ष पद्मनाभ सुरोत्तम । भक्तानाम् अनुरक्तानां त्राता भव जनार्दन ॥
blocks.te: విశాలమైన కమల నేత్రాలు గలవాడా, పద్మనాభా, దేవతలలో శ్రేష్ఠుడా, జనార్దనా — నిన్ను ప్రేమించే భక్తులకు నువ్వే రక్షకుడివి కావాలి.
blocks.en: O wide lotus-eyed, lotus-naveled, best of gods — O Janārdana, be the protector of Your devoted lovers.
blocks.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
blocks.split_iast: padmapatraviśālākṣa padmanābha surottama | bhaktānām anuraktānāṃ trātā bhava janārdana ||

sa: सोऽहमेकेन श्लोकेन स्तुत एव न संशयः ॥
notes: स्तोतुम् इच्छति: the infinitive with इच्छति "wishes to praise" (lesson 7.3).
सः अहम् "that I": the correlative सः agrees with the first-person अहम्. Sanskrit freely uses सः with अहम् or त्वम्: सोऽहम्.
स्तुतः is the past participle of स्तु; with एकेन श्लोकेन it means "(am) praised by a single verse". स्तुतः + एव → स्तुत एव (lesson 8.5).
blocks.split: यः मां नामसहस्रेण स्तोतुम् इच्छति पाण्डव । सः अहम् एकेन श्लोकेन स्तुतः एव न संशयः ॥
blocks.te: పాండవా, వెయ్యి నామాలతో నన్ను స్తుతించాలనుకునేవారు — ఒక్క శ్లోకంతో స్తుతించినా నేను స్తుతించబడినట్లే; ఇందులో సందేహం లేదు.
blocks.en: O Pāṇḍava, whoever wishes to praise Me with the thousand names — I am indeed praised even by a single verse; of this there is no doubt.
blocks.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
iast: so'hamekena ślokena stuta eva na saṃśayaḥ ||
blocks.split_iast: yaḥ māṃ nāmasahasreṇa stotum icchati pāṇḍava | saḥ aham ekena ślokena stutaḥ eva na saṃśayaḥ ||

sa: श्रीराम राम रामेति रमे रामे मनोरमे ।
notes: Three words ending in -ए, with three different grammars: रमे is a verb (रम्, ātmanepada, 1st singular present, "I delight"); रामे is a noun (locative of राम, "in Rāma"); वरानने is a vocative (feminine ā-stem, "O lovely-faced one").
मनोरमे can be taken two ways: as a locative agreeing with रामे ("in the charming Rāma"), or as a second vocative to Pārvatī ("O charming one"). Both readings are traditional.
Śiva is speaking to Pārvatī. सहस्रनाम is the neuter nominative of -नामन्; तत्तुल्यम् = तेन तुल्यम् "equal to that".
blocks.split: श्रीराम राम राम इति रमे रामे मनोरमे । सहस्रनाम तत्तुल्यं रामनाम वरानने ॥
blocks.anvaya: वरानने, "श्रीराम राम राम" इति (जपन्) मनोरमे रामे रमे । रामनाम सहस्रनाम-तत्तुल्यम् ॥
blocks.te: అందమైన ముఖం గలదానా, “రామ రామ రామ” అనే మనోహరమైన నామంలో నేను ఆనందిస్తాను; ఒక్క రామ నామం వెయ్యి నామాలకు సమానం.
blocks.en: O fair-faced one, I delight in the enchanting name "Rāma, Rāma, Rāma"; the single name Rāma is equal to the entire thousand names.
blocks.speaker: ईश्वर उवाच
iast: śrīrāma rāma rāmeti rame rāme manorame |
blocks.split_iast: śrīrāma rāma rāma iti rame rāme manorame | sahasranāma tattulyaṃ rāmanāma varānane ||
blocks.anvaya_iast: varānane, "śrīrāma rāma rāma" iti (japan) manorame rāme rame | rāmanāma sahasranāma-tattulyam ||

blocks.title: Telugu -ఏ and Sanskrit -ए
text: In Telugu, -ఏ at the end of a word is usually emphasis (రాముడే). In Sanskrit, -ए can be a 1st singular ātmanepada verb (रमे, वन्दे), a locative (रामे), a feminine vocative (देवि is -इ, but रमे, सीते are -ए), a dative ending (हरये) or a dual (फले). Always ask "which stem, which case?" before translating.

words: వేల పాదాలు, కన్నులు, శిరస్సులు, తొడలు, బాహువులు గలవానికి
notes: Datives of five stem types: -अ (अनन्ताय, पुरुषाय), -इ (सहस्रमूर्तये), -उ (बाहवे), -अन् (सहस्रनाम्ने: the अ of नामन् drops before -ए) and -इन् (धारिणे).
सहस्रपादाक्षिशिरोरुबाहवे: a dvandva of five body parts (पाद, अक्षि, शिरस्, ऊरु, बाहु) inside a bahuvrīhi with सहस्र- (lesson 9.5). The bahuvrīhi takes the last stem, बाहु, so the dative is -बाहवे.
न मोस् त्व · नन् ता य · स हस् र · मूर् त ये = ।ऽ। ऽऽ। ।ऽ। ऽ।ऽ: ज त ज र, twelve syllables, the वंशस्थ metre (lesson 12.4).
blocks.split: नमः अस्तु अनन्ताय सहस्रमूर्तये सहस्रपादाक्षिशिरोरुबाहवे । सहस्रनाम्ने पुरुषाय शाश्वते सहस्रकोटीयुगधारिणे नमः ॥
blocks.te: వేయి రూపాలు, పాదాలు, కళ్ళు, తలలు, చేతులు గలవాడు, వేయి నామాలు గలవాడు, వేల కోట్ల యుగాలను ధరించే శాశ్వత పురుషుడు అయిన అనంతునికి నమస్కారం.
blocks.en: Salutations to the Infinite — of a thousand forms, feet, eyes, heads, and arms; of a thousand names; the eternal Person who bears thousands of crores of yugas.
blocks.speaker: ब्रह्मोवाच
blocks.split_iast: namaḥ astu anantāya sahasramūrtaye sahasrapādākṣiśirorubāhave | sahasranāmne puruṣāya śāśvate sahasrakoṭīyugadhāriṇe namaḥ ||

sa: तत्सर्वं क्षम्यतां देव नारायण नमोऽस्तु ते ॥
notes: क्षम्यताम् is a passive imperative (lesson 6.8): passive stem क्षम्य- + the ātmanepada imperative ending -ताम्, "let it be forgiven". Polite Sanskrit prefers the passive: it does not order the god directly.
यत् … यत् … तत् सर्वम्: two relative clauses gathered by one correlative (lesson 11.3).
अक्षरपदभ्रष्टम्: अक्षरात् पदात् वा भ्रष्टम्, a pañcamī tatpuruṣa with a dvandva inside. मात्राहीनम्: मात्रया हीनम्, a tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa.
blocks.split: यत् अक्षरपदभ्रष्टं मात्राहीनं तु यत् भवेत् । तत् सर्वं क्षम्यतां देव नारायण नमः अस्तु ते ॥
blocks.te: నారాయణా, ఈ పారాయణంలో అక్షరం గానీ, పదం గానీ, ఛందస్సు గానీ తప్పుగా ఉంటే — అదంతా క్షమించు; నీకు నమస్కారం.
blocks.en: O Lord Nārāyaṇa, forgive whatever syllable, word, or metre may be faulty in this recitation — salutations to You.
blocks.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
iast: tatsarvaṃ kṣamyatāṃ deva nārāyaṇa namo'stu te ||
blocks.split_iast: yat akṣarapadabhraṣṭaṃ mātrāhīnaṃ tu yat bhavet | tat sarvaṃ kṣamyatāṃ deva nārāyaṇa namaḥ astu te ||

quiz.q: In "यः इदं शृणुयात् … न अशुभं प्राप्नुयात्", both verbs are:
quiz.why: The phala-śruti pattern: whoever would … would.
Passive stem मुच्य- + optative -एत.
A feminine consonant stem; the ablative with मुच्.

quiz.q: In Phala Śruti 14, why is विधृतानि neuter plural?
options: the subjects are of mixed genders
quiz.why: A shared adjective for mixed genders goes into the neuter plural.

quiz.q: In श्रीराम राम रामेति रमे, the word रमे is:
quiz.why: Read with रामे: "I delight in Rāma".
Passive imperative of क्षम्.
Twelve syllables: ।ऽ।ऽऽ।।ऽ।ऽ।ऽ.

lessons.title: స్తోత్రాలు · The great stotras
lessons.summary: Opening verses of the stotras heard in Telugu homes and temples: Śiva Pañcākṣara, Liṅgāṣṭakam, Madhurāṣṭakam, Mahālakṣmyaṣṭakam, the Hanumān and Rāma verses of the Rāmarakṣā, and the Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa Suprabhātam. Each is read word by word, with its metre and its grammar: datives, vocatives, accusatives with प्रपद्ये and नमामि, kṛt nouns with genitive objects, superlatives, and the imperative उत्तिष्ठ.

blocks.text: How a stotra is put together

blocks.title: Find the verb, then the case
text: A stotra verse usually has one verb or one नमः. Find it first. Then every epithet is in the case that verb wants: नमः → dative, नमामि / वन्दे / प्रपद्ये → accusative, नमः ते → vocative + ते. The epithets are almost always bahuvrīhis.

sa: नित्याय शुद्धाय दिगम्बराय तस्मै नकाराय नमः शिवाय ॥
notes: Every epithet is a dative in -आय, governed by नमः at the end (lesson 11.2). There are four bahuvrīhis: नागेन्द्रः हारः यस्य, त्रीणि लोचनानि यस्य, भस्म अङ्गरागः यस्य, दिशः अम्बरं यस्य.
नकार "the sound न": -कार after a letter names it (अकार, ककार, नकार). The five verses begin with न, म, शि, वा, य: नमः शिवाय, the pañcākṣarī.

ना गेन् द्र · हा रा य · त्रि लो च · ना य = ऽऽ। ऽऽ। ।ऽ। ऽऽ: त त ज ग ग, the इन्द्रवज्रा (lesson 12.3). The य before त्रि is counted light: poets often allow this before a word beginning with a conjunct in र.
blocks.title: शिवपञ्चाक्षरस्तोत्रम् 1 (attributed to Śaṅkara)
blocks.split: नागेन्द्रहाराय त्रिलोचनाय भस्माङ्गरागाय महेश्वराय । नित्याय शुद्धाय दिगम्बराय तस्मै नकाराय नमः शिवाय ॥
blocks.te: సర్పరాజును హారంగా, విభూతిని అంగరాగంగా ధరించిన త్రినేత్రుడు, మహేశ్వరుడు, నిత్యుడు, శుద్ధుడు, దిగంబరుడు, "న" కార స్వరూపుడు అయిన ఆ శివునికి నమస్కారం.
blocks.en: To him who wears the king of serpents as a garland, the three-eyed, whose body-paint is sacred ash, the great lord, eternal, pure, clothed by the directions: to that Śiva, who is the syllable "na", salutations.
iast: nityāya śuddhāya digambarāya tasmai nakārāya namaḥ śivāya ||
blocks.split_iast: nāgendrahārāya trilocanāya bhasmāṅgarāgāya maheśvarāya | nityāya śuddhāya digambarāya tasmai nakārāya namaḥ śivāya ||

words: జన్మ వల్ల కలిగే దుఃఖాన్ని నశింపజేసే లింగాన్ని
notes: ब्रह्ममुरारिसुरार्चित: a dvandva (ब्रह्मा च मुरारिः च सुराः च) inside a tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa with the past participle अर्चित "worshipped by" (lesson 9.5).
जन्मजदुःखविनाशक: जन्मनः जातं दुःखम् (upapada -ज), तस्य विनाशकम्. -अक is a kṛt suffix for agents (ण्वुल्, lesson 7.5): विनाशक "destroyer", like पाठक, गायक.
प्रणमामि takes the accusative, so every लिङ्गम् is 2nd case. The metre counts mātrās (16 per quarter), like Bhaja Govindam (lesson 13.11).
blocks.title: लिङ्गाष्टकम् 1
blocks.split: ब्रह्ममुरारिसुरार्चितलिङ्गं निर्मलभासितशोभितलिङ्गम् । जन्मजदुःखविनाशकलिङ्गं तत् प्रणमामि सदाशिवलिङ्गम् ॥
blocks.te: బ్రహ్మ, విష్ణువు, దేవతలచే పూజించబడినది, నిర్మలమైన కాంతితో శోభించేది, జన్మ దుఃఖాన్ని నశింపజేసేది అయిన ఆ సదాశివ లింగానికి నమస్కరిస్తున్నాను.
blocks.en: The liṅga worshipped by Brahmā, Viṣṇu and the gods, radiant with pure light, destroyer of the sorrow born of birth: to that Sadāśiva liṅga I bow.
blocks.split_iast: brahmamurārisurārcitaliṅgaṃ nirmalabhāsitaśobhitaliṅgam | janmajaduḥkhavināśakaliṅgaṃ tat praṇamāmi sadāśivaliṅgam ||

sa: अधरं मधुरं वदनं मधुरं नयनं मधुरं हसितं मधुरम् ।
हृदयं मधुरं गमनं मधुरं मधुराधिपतेरखिलं मधुरम् ॥
notes: The simplest grammar in all the stotras: nominal sentences "X (is) sweet" (lesson 2.5). Every noun is neuter, so मधुरम् is neuter too.
अ ध रं · म धु रं · व द नं · म धु रं = ।।ऽ ।।ऽ ।।ऽ ।।ऽ: four स gaṇas, the तोटक metre (lesson 12.4).
हसितम् and गमनम् are verbal nouns: हसित is a past participle used as a noun "smiling" (lesson 7.1); गमन is a kṛt noun in -अन "going" (lesson 7.5).
मधुराधिपतेः is the genitive of the i-stem अधिपति, with guṇa: -एः (lesson 4.5). One genitive at the very end belongs to every noun in the verse.
blocks.title: मधुराष्टकम् 1 (Vallabhācārya)
blocks.split: अधरं मधुरं वदनं मधुरं नयनं मधुरं हसितं मधुरम् । हृदयं मधुरं गमनं मधुरं मधुराधिपतेः अखिलं मधुरम् ॥
blocks.te: మధురాధిపతి అయిన కృష్ణుని పెదవి మధురం, ముఖం మధురం, కన్నులు మధురం, నవ్వు మధురం, హృదయం మధురం, నడక మధురం — ఆయనకు సంబంధించిన సమస్తం మధురం.
blocks.en: His lips are sweet, his face is sweet, his eyes are sweet, his smile is sweet; his heart is sweet, his gait is sweet: everything about the lord of Mathurā is sweet.
iast: adharaṃ madhuraṃ vadanaṃ madhuraṃ nayanaṃ madhuraṃ hasitaṃ madhuram |
hṛdayaṃ madhuraṃ gamanaṃ madhuraṃ madhurādhipaterakhilaṃ madhuram ||
blocks.split_iast: adharaṃ madhuraṃ vadanaṃ madhuraṃ nayanaṃ madhuraṃ hasitaṃ madhuram | hṛdayaṃ madhuraṃ gamanaṃ madhuraṃ madhurādhipateḥ akhilaṃ madhuram ||

notes: Five feminine vocatives: four in -ए from ā-stems (महामाये, श्रीपीठे, सुरपूजिते, शङ्खचक्रगदाहस्ते), one in short -इ from the ई-stem लक्ष्मी (lesson 4.4).
सुरपूजिते is a past participle "worshipped by the gods" (tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa) in the feminine vocative. शङ्खचक्रगदाहस्ते: a dvandva inside a bahuvrīhi, शङ्खचक्रगदाः हस्ते यस्याः सा.
नमः ते अस्तु: the vocatives come between the dative ते and the end; both halves say the same thing.
blocks.title: महालक्ष्म्यष्टकम् 1 (Indra's hymn, Padma Purāṇa)
blocks.split: नमः ते अस्तु महामाये श्रीपीठे सुरपूजिते । शङ्खचक्रगदाहस्ते महालक्ष्मि नमः अस्तु ते ॥
blocks.te: ఓ మహామాయా, శ్రీపీఠంపై వెలసినదానా, దేవతలచే పూజించబడినదానా, శంఖ చక్ర గదలు చేతుల్లో గలదానా, ఓ మహాలక్ష్మీ, నీకు నమస్కారం.
blocks.en: Salutations to you, O great Māyā, seated on the throne of Śrī, worshipped by the gods; O Mahālakṣmī with conch, discus and mace in your hands, salutations to you.
blocks.split_iast: namaḥ te astu mahāmāye śrīpīṭhe surapūjite | śaṅkhacakragadāhaste mahālakṣmi namaḥ astu te ||

notes: प्रपद्ये (प्र + पद्, ātmanepada, 1st singular) with शरणम्: "I go for refuge to". It takes the accusative, so all seven epithets are 2nd case.
बुद्धिमतां वरिष्ठम्: the partitive genitive (बुद्धिमत्, -मत् stem, genitive plural) with वरिष्ठ, the superlative of उरु "broad, great" (lesson 10.2).
मनोजवम्: मनसः इव जवः यस्य, a bahuvrīhi with a comparison. जितेन्द्रियम्: जितानि इन्द्रियाणि येन सः. वातात्मजम्: वातस्य आत्मजः, a tatpuruṣa.
म नो ज · वं मा रु · त तुल् य · वे गं = ।ऽ। ऽऽ। ।ऽ। ऽऽ, an उपेन्द्रवज्रा line. With इन्द्रवज्रा lines it makes उपजाति (lesson 12.3).
blocks.title: श्रीरामरक्षास्तोत्रम् 33
blocks.split: मनोजवं मारुततुल्यवेगं जितेन्द्रियं बुद्धिमतां वरिष्ठम् । वातात्मजं वानरयूथमुख्यं श्रीरामदूतं शरणं प्रपद्ये ॥
blocks.te: మనోవేగం గలవాడు, వాయువేగం గలవాడు, ఇంద్రియాలను జయించినవాడు, బుద్ధిమంతులలో శ్రేష్ఠుడు, వాయుపుత్రుడు, వానర సేనాధిపతి అయిన శ్రీరామదూతను శరణు పొందుతున్నాను.
blocks.en: I take refuge in the messenger of Śrī Rāma: swift as the mind, fast as the wind, master of the senses, foremost of the wise, son of the Wind, chief of the monkey hosts.
blocks.split_iast: manojavaṃ mārutatulyavegaṃ jitendriyaṃ buddhimatāṃ variṣṭham | vātātmajaṃ vānarayūthamukhyaṃ śrīrāmadūtaṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadye ||

notes: अपहर्तारम् and दातारम् are agent nouns in -तृ, accusative (lesson 7.5). Their objects are in the 6th case: आपदाम्, सर्वसम्पदाम् (genitive plurals of the feminine consonant stems आपद्, सम्पद्).
भूयः is the comparative of बहु "more", used as an adverb; doubled, भूयो भूयः means "again and again".
नमामि takes the accusative, unlike नमः, which takes the dative.
blocks.title: श्रीरामरक्षास्तोत्रम् 35
blocks.split: आपदाम् अपहर्तारं दातारं सर्वसम्पदाम् । लोकाभिरामं श्रीरामं भूयः भूयः नमामि अहम् ॥
blocks.te: ఆపదలను తొలగించేవాడు, సమస్త సంపదలను ఇచ్చేవాడు, లోకానికి ఆనందాన్ని ఇచ్చేవాడు అయిన శ్రీరామునికి మళ్ళీ మళ్ళీ నమస్కరిస్తున్నాను.
blocks.en: To the remover of distress, the giver of all wealth, the delight of the world, Śrī Rāma, I bow again and again.
blocks.split_iast: āpadām apahartāraṃ dātāraṃ sarvasampadām | lokābhirāmaṃ śrīrāmaṃ bhūyaḥ bhūyaḥ namāmi aham ||

notes: वेधसे is the dative of the -अस् stem वेधस् "creator". सीतायाः is the genitive of the ā-stem सीता (lesson 4.4).
पतये: Pāṇini's grammar gives पत्ये for पति "husband" standing alone, and पतये only in compounds (पतिः समास एव, Aṣṭādhyāyī 1.4.8). Stotras often use पतये anyway; recognise both.
blocks.title: traditional Rāma verse
blocks.split: रामाय रामभद्राय रामचन्द्राय वेधसे । रघुनाथाय नाथाय सीतायाः पतये नमः ॥
blocks.te: రామునికి, రామభద్రునికి, రామచంద్రునికి, సృష్టికర్తకు, రఘునాథునికి, నాథునికి, సీతాపతికి నమస్కారం.
blocks.en: To Rāma, Rāmabhadra, Rāmacandra, the creator, the lord of the Raghus, the lord, the husband of Sītā: salutations.
blocks.split_iast: rāmāya rāmabhadrāya rāmacandrāya vedhase | raghunāthāya nāthāya sītāyāḥ pataye namaḥ ||

blocks.text: The Suprabhātam sung at Tirumala opens with a verse from the Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa (Bālakāṇḍa 23.2), where Viśvāmitra wakes the young Rāma.

words: కౌసల్య మంచి సంతానం గలది (నీ వంటి కుమారుడు గలది)
notes: सुप्रजाः: प्रजा becomes -प्रजस् at the end of a bahuvrīhi (नित्यमसिच् प्रजामेधयोः, Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.4.122): शोभना प्रजा यस्याः सा सुप्रजाः. Before राम the visarga drops: सुप्रजा राम. Many readers take कौसल्यासुप्रजाः as one compound addressed to Rāma; the split above follows the usual Rāmāyaṇa commentaries.
उत्तिष्ठ = उद् + स्था, imperative. The स् of स्था is lost after उद् (उदः स्थास्तम्भोः पूर्वस्य, Aṣṭādhyāyī 8.4.61), and स्था has the present stem तिष्ठ (lesson 6.3).
कर्तव्यम् is a gerundive "must be done" (lesson 7.4). दैवम् and आह्निकम् are taddhitas with vṛddhi: from देव, and from अहन् "day" (lesson 10.2).
नरशार्दूल: नरः शार्दूलः इव, a comparison compound, "a tiger among men".
blocks.title: श्रीवेङ्कटेशसुप्रभातम् 1 (Rāmāyaṇa 1.23.2)
blocks.split: कौसल्या सुप्रजाः राम पूर्वा सन्ध्या प्रवर्तते । उत्तिष्ठ नरशार्दूल कर्तव्यं दैवम् आह्निकम् ॥
blocks.te: ఓ రామా, కౌసల్య నీ వంటి మంచి కుమారుని పొందింది. ప్రాతః సంధ్య వస్తోంది. ఓ నరశార్దూలా, లే; దైవ సంబంధమైన నిత్య కర్మలు చేయవలసి ఉంది.
blocks.en: Rāma, Kausalyā has a worthy son in you. The morning twilight is coming. Rise, tiger among men: the daily rites to the gods must be done.
blocks.split_iast: kausalyā suprajāḥ rāma pūrvā sandhyā pravartate | uttiṣṭha naraśārdūla kartavyaṃ daivam āhnikam ||

notes: Three masculine vocatives in -अ: गोविन्द, गरुडध्वज (bahuvrīhi: गरुडः ध्वजे यस्य), कमलाकान्त (tatpuruṣa: कमलायाः कान्तः).
उत्तिष्ठ + उत्तिष्ठ → उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ (a + u → o). But गोविन्द उत्तिष्ठ stays apart: verse often leaves a vowel unjoined after a vocative, at a natural pause.
त्रैलोक्यम्: त्रयः लोकाः = त्रिलोकी; with the taddhita -य and vṛddhi it becomes the collective noun त्रैलोक्य "the three worlds". कुरु takes two accusatives: "make the three worlds auspicious".
blocks.title: श्रीवेङ्कटेशसुप्रभातम् 2
blocks.split: उत्तिष्ठ उत्तिष्ठ गोविन्द उत्तिष्ठ गरुडध्वज । उत्तिष्ठ कमलाकान्त त्रैलोक्यं मङ्गलं कुरु ॥
blocks.te: లే, లే గోవిందా! లే, గరుడధ్వజా! లే, కమలాకాంతా! మూడు లోకాలకు మంగళం చేయి.
blocks.en: Rise, rise, Govinda! Rise, you whose banner bears Garuḍa! Rise, beloved of Kamalā, and make the three worlds auspicious.
blocks.split_iast: uttiṣṭha uttiṣṭha govinda uttiṣṭha garuḍadhvaja | uttiṣṭha kamalākānta trailokyaṃ maṅgalaṃ kuru ||

blocks.title: Suprabhātam in Telugu homes
text: Many Telugu families play the Suprabhātam at dawn. Now that you can parse it, try the next verses on your own: they use the same vocatives, more imperatives (उत्तिष्ठ, जागृहि) and long bahuvrīhis for Veṅkaṭeśa. Read each verse with the method of lesson 11.5.

quiz.q: In the Śiva Pañcākṣara, the epithets are in the dative because of:
quiz.why: नमः takes the 4th case.
-कार names a letter.
ण्वुल्, like पाठक "reader".

quiz.q: In the Madhurāṣṭakam, मधुरम् is neuter because:
quiz.why: An adjective agrees with its noun.
Partitive genitive with a superlative.

quiz.q: अपहर्तारम् takes its object (आपदाम्) in which case?
quiz.why: A kṛt noun's object goes into the 6th case.
पतिः समास एव: पति is like हरि only in compounds.
The स् of स्था drops after उद्.

lessons.title: భజ గోవిందం · Bhaja Govindam
lessons.summary: Śaṅkara's Moha-mudgara, read verse by verse: the refrain and nine stanzas, with their rhyming mātrā metre. Grammar: the irregular imperatives जहीहि, विद्धि, पाहि; मा + imperative; a chain of locatives; past participles with an active sense; the future द्रक्ष्यसि; and the grammar joke at the heart of the poem, डुकृञ् करणे.

blocks.text: A grammar joke at the start

Tradition says Śaṅkara, walking in Kāśī, heard an old scholar learning Pāṇini's list of roots by heart: "डुकृञ् करणे, डुकृञ् करणे …". He sang the refrain: when death is near, डुकृञ् करणे will not save you; sing of Govinda.
डुकृञ् करणे is the actual dhātupāṭha entry for the root कृ (lesson 6.2). The extra letters are markers (इत्), not part of the root:

head: Part
What it is
What it tells you
rows: the root is ubhayapada: करोति and कुरुते
iast: the root is ubhayapada: karoti and kurute

blocks.title: The verse that mocks grammar teaches it
text: The refrain mocks memorising rules without devotion. But to understand the joke you need to know the dhātupāṭha. Learn both: the rule and the Govinda.

blocks.text: The refrain itself (भज गोविन्दं भज गोविन्दं) was scanned in lesson 12.1. The metre counts mātrās, 16 to each quarter, and the two halves of each verse rhyme at the end (అంత్యప్రాస). Telugu padyams rhyme on the second syllable instead (ప్రాస, lesson 12.4).
Give up the thirst for wealth

sa: मूढ जहीहि धनागमतृष्णां कुरु सद्बुद्धिं मनसि वितृष्णाम् ।
यल्लभसे निजकर्मोपात्तं वित्तं तेन विनोदय चित्तम् ॥
notes: जहीहि is the imperative of हा "abandon" (class 3), an irregular form. कुरु is the imperative of कृ, and विनोदय is a causative imperative (वि + नुद्, "make glad", lesson 6.9).
लभसे is the ātmanepada present, 2nd singular, of लभ् (lesson 6.1). यत् + लभसे → यल्लभसे (त् before ल becomes ल्, lesson 8.3).
उपात्त = उप + आ + दा, past participle "obtained" (दा → -त्त after a prefix). वितृष्णाम् is a feminine bahuvrīhi agreeing with सद्बुद्धिम्.
blocks.split: मूढ जहीहि धनागमतृष्णां कुरु सद्बुद्धिं मनसि वितृष्णाम् । यत् लभसे निजकर्मोपात्तं वित्तं तेन विनोदय चित्तम् ॥
blocks.anvaya: मूढ, धनागमतृष्णां जहीहि; मनसि वितृष्णां सद्बुद्धिं कुरु । निजकर्मोपात्तं यत् वित्तं लभसे, तेन चित्तं विनोदय ॥
blocks.en: O fool, give up your thirst for amassing wealth; cultivate a wise, desireless mind. Be content with whatever wealth comes to you through the fruits of your own past deeds.
iast: mūḍha jahīhi dhanāgamatṛṣṇāṃ kuru sadbuddhiṃ manasi vitṛṣṇām |
yallabhase nijakarmopāttaṃ vittaṃ tena vinodaya cittam ||
blocks.split_iast: mūḍha jahīhi dhanāgamatṛṣṇāṃ kuru sadbuddhiṃ manasi vitṛṣṇām | yat labhase nijakarmopāttaṃ vittaṃ tena vinodaya cittam ||
blocks.anvaya_iast: mūḍha, dhanāgamatṛṣṇāṃ jahīhi; manasi vitṛṣṇāṃ sadbuddhiṃ kuru | nijakarmopāttaṃ yat vittaṃ labhase, tena cittaṃ vinodaya ||

blocks.text: Life is a drop on a lotus leaf

sa: विद्धि व्याध्यभिमानग्रस्तं लोकं शोकहतं च समस्तम् ॥
notes: The lotus leaf again (Gītā 5.10, lesson 13.4), but now for how short life is: the drop runs off in a moment.
विद्धि is the irregular imperative of विद् "know" (class 2). It takes two accusatives: "know the world (as) seized by disease".
तद्वत् "like that": -वत् makes a comparison adverb (lesson 10.2). तद्वत् + जीवितम् → तद्वज्जीवितम् (त् + ज → ज्ज, lesson 8.3).
blocks.split: नलिनीदलगतजलम् अतितरलं तद्वत् जीवितम् अतिशयचपलम् । विद्धि व्याध्यभिमानग्रस्तं लोकं शोकहतं च समस्तम् ॥
blocks.anvaya: नलिनीदलगतजलम् अतितरलम्; तद्वत् जीवितम् अतिशयचपलम् । समस्तं लोकं व्याध्यभिमानग्रस्तं शोकहतं च विद्धि ॥
blocks.en: Life is as unstable as a drop of water trembling upon a lotus petal — exceedingly fickle. Know that the entire world is seized by disease and pride, and is struck through and through by grief.
iast: viddhi vyādhyabhimānagrastaṃ lokaṃ śokahataṃ ca samastam ||
blocks.split_iast: nalinīdalagatajalam atitaralaṃ tadvat jīvitam atiśayacapalam | viddhi vyādhyabhimānagrastaṃ lokaṃ śokahataṃ ca samastam ||
blocks.anvaya_iast: nalinīdalagatajalam atitaralam; tadvat jīvitam atiśayacapalam | samastaṃ lokaṃ vyādhyabhimānagrastaṃ śokahataṃ ca viddhi ||

sa: वृद्धस्तावच्चिन्तासक्तः परमे ब्रह्मणि कोऽपि न सक्तः ॥
notes: Three saptamī tatpuruṣas with the past participle आसक्त "attached": क्रीडायाम् आसक्तः, तरुण्याम् आसक्तः, चिन्तायाम् आसक्तः (lesson 9.2). Then the same idea without a compound: परमे ब्रह्मणि … सक्तः, with the locative.
कः अपि न "no one at all" (lesson 5.3). कः + अपि → कोऽपि.
Sandhi: बालः + तावत् → बालस्तावत्; तावत् + च → तावच्च (lesson 8.3).
blocks.split: बालः तावत् क्रीडासक्तः तरुणः तावत् तरुणीसक्तः । वृद्धः तावत् चिन्तासक्तः परमे ब्रह्मणि कः अपि न सक्तः ॥
blocks.en: The child is absorbed in play, the youth is absorbed in the pursuit of women, and the aged is absorbed in worries — but hardly anyone becomes absorbed in the Supreme Brahman.
iast: vṛddhastāvaccintāsaktaḥ parame brahmaṇi ko'pi na saktaḥ ||
blocks.split_iast: bālaḥ tāvat krīḍāsaktaḥ taruṇaḥ tāvat taruṇīsaktaḥ | vṛddhaḥ tāvat cintāsaktaḥ parame brahmaṇi kaḥ api na saktaḥ ||

blocks.text: Who is your wife, who is your son?

sa: का ते कान्ता कस्ते पुत्रः संसारोऽयमतीव विचित्रः ।
कस्य त्वं कः कुत आयातस्तत्त्वं चिन्तय तदिह भ्रातः ॥
notes: किम् in three forms: का (feminine, agreeing with कान्ता), कः (masculine), कस्य (genitive): lesson 5.3. The questions have no verbs.
आयातः "(you) have come" is a past participle with an active meaning: verbs of motion make active past participles (गत्यर्थाकर्मक…, Aṣṭādhyāyī 3.4.72; lesson 7.1).
भ्रातः is the vocative of the ṛ-stem भ्रातृ (lesson 4.7). चिन्तय is a class 10 imperative.
blocks.split: का ते कान्ता कः ते पुत्रः संसारः अयम् अतीव विचित्रः । कस्य त्वं कः कुतः आयातः तत्त्वं चिन्तय तत् इह भ्रातः ॥
blocks.en: Who is your wife? Who is your son? This samsara is exceedingly strange. Whose are you? Who are you? Where have you come from? Ponder this truth, O brother, here and now.
iast: kā te kāntā kaste putraḥ saṃsāro'yamatīva vicitraḥ |
kasya tvaṃ kaḥ kuta āyātastattvaṃ cintaya tadiha bhrātaḥ ||
blocks.split_iast: kā te kāntā kaḥ te putraḥ saṃsāraḥ ayam atīva vicitraḥ | kasya tvaṃ kaḥ kutaḥ āyātaḥ tattvaṃ cintaya tat iha bhrātaḥ ||

notes: A chain of locative absolutes with no participle: "when there is X, Y (arises)"; सति "being" is understood (lesson 11.4).
The mirror image of Gītā 2.62–63 (lesson 13.3). There the ladder goes down, with ablatives; here it goes up, with locatives.
-त्व makes abstract nouns (lesson 10.2): सत्सङ्गत्व "being in good company". जीवन्मुक्तिः: जीवन् "while living" (present participle) + मुक्ति.
blocks.split: सत्सङ्गत्वे निस्सङ्गत्वं निस्सङ्गत्वे निर्मोहत्वम् । निर्मोहत्वे निश्चलतत्त्वं निश्चलतत्त्वे जीवन्मुक्तिः ॥
blocks.en: From good company comes non-attachment; from non-attachment comes freedom from delusion; from freedom from delusion comes steadfastness in the Truth; and from steadfastness in the Truth comes liberation while yet living.
blocks.split_iast: satsaṅgatve nissaṅgatvaṃ nissaṅgatve nirmohatvam | nirmohatve niścalatattvaṃ niścalatattve jīvanmuktiḥ ||

blocks.title: Two ladders
text: Down (Gītā 2.62–63), ablatives: ध्यानात् सङ्गः, सङ्गात् कामः, … Up (Bhaja Govindam 9), locatives: सत्सङ्गत्वे निस्सङ्गत्वम्, … Learn them as a pair. The cases tell you the direction: -आत् "from" falls, -ए "when there is" climbs.

sa: मा कुरु धनजनयौवनगर्वं हरति निमेषात्कालः सर्वम् ।
मायामयमिदमखिलं हित्वा ब्रह्मपदं त्वं प्रविश विदित्वा ॥
notes: मा कुरु: मा with the imperative for "don't". Pāṇini pairs मा with the aorist (मा कार्षीः); later Sanskrit uses मा + imperative freely (lesson 6.6).
हित्वा is the irregular absolutive of हा (lesson 7.3); विदित्वा is the absolutive of विद् with the connecting इ.
निमेषात् "within a blink" is an ablative of time. मायामयम्: -मय "made of" (lesson 10.2).
blocks.split: मा कुरु धनजनयौवनगर्वं हरति निमेषात् कालः सर्वम् । मायामयम् इदम् अखिलं हित्वा ब्रह्मपदं त्वं प्रविश विदित्वा ॥
blocks.anvaya: धनजनयौवनगर्वं मा कुरु; कालः निमेषात् सर्वं हरति । इदम् अखिलं मायामयं विदित्वा हित्वा (च), त्वं ब्रह्मपदं प्रविश ॥
blocks.en: Do not take pride in wealth, followers, and youth — time snatches all of it away in an instant. Giving up this entirely illusory world, enter the state of Brahman having truly known it.
iast: mā kuru dhanajanayauvanagarvaṃ harati nimeṣātkālaḥ sarvam |
māyāmayamidamakhilaṃ hitvā brahmapadaṃ tvaṃ praviśa viditvā ||
blocks.split_iast: mā kuru dhanajanayauvanagarvaṃ harati nimeṣāt kālaḥ sarvam | māyāmayam idam akhilaṃ hitvā brahmapadaṃ tvaṃ praviśa viditvā ||
blocks.anvaya_iast: dhanajanayauvanagarvaṃ mā kuru; kālaḥ nimeṣāt sarvaṃ harati | idam akhilaṃ māyāmayaṃ viditvā hitvā (ca), tvaṃ brahmapadaṃ praviśa ||

sa: सकृदपि येन मुरारिसमर्चा क्रियते तस्य यमेन न चर्चा ॥
notes: One relative pronoun, येन, serves three passive clauses: two past participles (अधीता, पीता, feminine to agree with गीता and कणिका) and one present passive (क्रियते, lesson 6.8).
अधीता is the past participle of अधि + इ "study". पीता is from पा "drink" (lesson 7.1).
The point for a learner: this course has asked you to read some of the Gītā. That counts.
blocks.split: भगवद्गीता किञ्चित् अधीता गङ्गाजललवकणिका पीता । सकृत् अपि येन मुरारिसमर्चा क्रियते तस्य यमेन न चर्चा ॥
blocks.anvaya: येन भगवद्गीता किञ्चित् अधीता, (येन) गङ्गाजललवकणिका पीता, (येन) सकृत् अपि मुरारिसमर्चा क्रियते, तस्य यमेन चर्चा न (भवति) ॥
blocks.en: For one who has studied even a little of the Bhagavad Gita, drunk even a tiny drop of Ganga water, and worshipped Murari even once — for him there is no reckoning to fear from Yama, the lord of death.
iast: sakṛdapi yena murārisamarcā kriyate tasya yamena na carcā ||
blocks.split_iast: bhagavadgītā kiñcit adhītā gaṅgājalalavakaṇikā pītā | sakṛt api yena murārisamarcā kriyate tasya yamena na carcā ||
blocks.anvaya_iast: yena bhagavadgītā kiñcit adhītā, (yena) gaṅgājalalavakaṇikā pītā, (yena) sakṛt api murārisamarcā kriyate, tasya yamena carcā na (bhavati) ||

sa: पुनरपि जननं पुनरपि मरणं पुनरपि जननीजठरे शयनम् ।
इह संसारे बहुदुस्तारे कृपयाऽपारे पाहि मुरारे ॥
notes: जनन, मरण, शयन are kṛt nouns in -अन "the act of" (lesson 7.5). The first line is nominal: three subjects, no verb.
संसारे बहुदुस्तारे अपारे: one noun and two adjectives in the locative. दुस्तार "hard to cross" is दुर् + तॄ with खल्, like दुर्लभ (lesson 13.5).
पाहि is the imperative of पा "protect" (class 2). मुरारे is the vocative of the i-stem मुरारि, with guṇa. कृपया is an instrumental "out of compassion".
blocks.split: पुनः अपि जननं पुनः अपि मरणं पुनः अपि जननीजठरे शयनम् । इह संसारे बहुदुस्तारे कृपया अपारे पाहि मुरारे ॥
blocks.en: Birth again, death again, and again lying within a mother's womb — this boundless samsara is so hard to cross. O Murari, protect me through Your mercy.
iast: punarapi jananaṃ punarapi maraṇaṃ punarapi jananījaṭhare śayanam |
iha saṃsāre bahudustāre kṛpayā'pāre pāhi murāre ||
blocks.split_iast: punaḥ api jananaṃ punaḥ api maraṇaṃ punaḥ api jananījaṭhare śayanam | iha saṃsāre bahudustāre kṛpayā apāre pāhi murāre ||

blocks.text: The last verse: devotion to the guru

notes: भव मुक्तः "be free": the imperative भव with a past participle as predicate.
द्रक्ष्यसि is the future of दृश् "see". The root changes to द्रक्ष्- (lesson 6.5). अचिरात् "before long" is an ablative used as an adverb.
सेन्द्रियमानसनियमात्: स- "together with" + इन्द्रिय + मानस + नियम, an ablative of cause. निजहृदयस्थम्: an upapada with -स्थ (lesson 9.2).
blocks.split: गुरुचरणाम्बुजनिर्भरभक्तः संसारात् अचिरात् भव मुक्तः । सेन्द्रियमानसनियमात् एवं द्रक्ष्यसि निजहृदयस्थं देवम् ॥
blocks.anvaya: गुरुचरणाम्बुजनिर्भरभक्तः (सन्) अचिरात् संसारात् मुक्तः भव । एवं सेन्द्रियमानसनियमात् निजहृदयस्थं देवं द्रक्ष्यसि ॥
blocks.en: O devotee wholly devoted to the lotus feet of the Guru, become free from samsara without delay. Through such discipline of the senses and the mind, you shall behold the Lord who dwells within your own heart.
blocks.split_iast: gurucaraṇāmbujanirbharabhaktaḥ saṃsārāt acirāt bhava muktaḥ | sendriyamānasaniyamāt evaṃ drakṣyasi nijahṛdayasthaṃ devam ||
blocks.anvaya_iast: gurucaraṇāmbujanirbharabhaktaḥ (san) acirāt saṃsārāt muktaḥ bhava | evaṃ sendriyamānasaniyamāt nijahṛdayasthaṃ devaṃ drakṣyasi ||

quiz.q: In डुकृञ् करणे, the -ञ् tells you:
quiz.why: A marker (इत्) after the root.
Class 3, irregular.
Imperative of विद्, class 2.

options: a locative: "when there is good company"
quiz.why: A locative absolute with सति understood.

quiz.q: आयातः "(you) have come" is active because:
options: past participles of motion verbs can be active
quiz.why: Aṣṭādhyāyī 3.4.72.
दृश् → द्रक्ष्-.

quiz.q: In verse 20, how many clauses does येन serve?
quiz.why: अधीता, पीता, क्रियते all take येन as the agent.

units.title: జ్ఞాపకం · Remembering it all
units.summary: How to keep the whole course in memory: the traditional Indian methods (chanting tables, kārikās, kaṇṭhapāṭha) and the modern ones (spaced repetition, active recall), one anchor verse for every major rule, one-page cheat sheets, and a twelve-month study plan with an honest map of what the course covers.

lessons.title: జ్ఞాపక పద్ధతులు · How to remember grammar
lessons.summary: Why Sanskrit grammar is easier to remember than it looks, the methods of the pāṭhaśālā (chanting, kārikās, Pāṇini's own compression tricks), the methods of memory research (spaced repetition, active recall, interleaving), how the app's six review boxes work, and an anchor verse for every major rule.

blocks.text: Sanskrit was built to be memorised
For two thousand years Sanskrit grammar was learned without books. Pāṇini wrote his grammar for memory, and the tradition built a whole set of techniques around it. You can use the same ones.

head: Technique
What it is
Where you met it
rows: rules compressed to a few syllables
one syllable naming a whole group of sounds (अच्, हल्, यण्)
a word stated once is understood in the rules that follow
a verse summary of a topic
chanting noun and verb tables daily
learning verses by heart before analysing them
iast: one syllable naming a whole group of sounds (ac, hal, yaṇ)

blocks.text: An example of अनुवृत्ति: इको यणचि (6.1.77) says "इ उ ऋ ऌ become य व र ल before a vowel". The next rule, एचोऽयवायावः (6.1.78), says only "ए ओ ऐ औ become अय् अव् आय् आव्". It does not repeat "before a vowel": अचि carries over from the rule before. Pāṇini's 4000 rules are short because most of their words are inherited this way.

blocks.title: Brevity is the point
text: Grammarians say they rejoice at saving half a short vowel as much as at the birth of a son (अर्धमात्रालाघवेन पुत्रोत्सवं मन्यन्ते वैयाकरणाः). Every rule in this course has been reduced to something you can say in one breath. Say it aloud; don't just read it.

blocks.text: The pāṭhaśālā method: chant, then understand

items: **Chant the table.** Say each noun table in rows of three (singular, dual, plural), case by case: रामः रामौ रामाः · रामं रामौ रामान् … Chant each verb table in rows of three, person by person: भवति भवतः भवन्ति · भवसि भवथः भवथ · भवामि भवावः भवामः.
**Chant the kārikā.** Learn the summary verses by heart: the ten classes (भ्वाद्यदादी …), the ten lakāras (लट् वर्तमाने …), the anuṣṭubh rule (पञ्चमं लघु सर्वत्र …).
**Learn a verse that uses the rule.** A rule without an example fades. A rule tied to a verse you can recite stays.
**Only then analyse.** Understanding comes faster when the forms are already in your mouth.

blocks.title: You did this already
text: Telugu schools teach the vibhakti list by chanting: "డుముపులు ప్రథమా విభక్తి, నిన్ నున్ లన్ గూర్చి గురించి ద్వితీయా విభక్తి…". You still remember it decades later. The Sanskrit tables work the same way: chant them until they are as automatic as డుముపులు.

head: Method
What to do
Why it works
rows: review a card just before you would forget it, at growing gaps
each successful recall makes the memory last longer
cover the answer and produce it yourself; then check
recalling strengthens memory far more than re-reading
mix card types (nouns, verbs, sandhi, verses) in one session
you learn to recognise which rule applies, not just the rule
connect each new form to something you know (Telugu, a verse)
connected memories are easier to find
review before sleeping; test the next morning
20 minutes daily beats 3 hours on Sunday
spacing is built into the habit

blocks.text: Every table row, worked verse and memory aid in the course becomes a card. The app keeps each card in one of six boxes:

head: Box
Next review
How a card gets there
rows: right three times, or marked "Known" in Learn mode
right five times; it stays here while you keep answering right

blocks.title: Be honest with the button
text: The boxes only work if you mark a card wrong when you hesitated or guessed. A wrongly marked "right" sends a weak card away for weeks. When in doubt, press wrong: it costs you one extra review tomorrow.

blocks.text: A good daily routine with the app:

items: **Due today** first: clear every due card (10–15 minutes).
**New** cards from the lesson you are studying (5–10 a day is plenty).
**Marked for review**: the cards you flagged as hard.
Once a week, take the quizzes of the last few lessons again.

blocks.text: The Telugu bridge as a memory tool
About half of literary Telugu vocabulary is Sanskrit (tatsama or tadbhava). Use it:

items: **Know the stem from Telugu.** Telugu రాముడు, వనము, సీత, హరి, గురువు, రాజు, మనస్సు give you the Sanskrit stems राम, वन, सीता, हरि, गुरु, राजन्, मनस्. The Telugu ending even tells you the stem type (lesson 0.2).
**Use Telugu compounds.** దేవాలయం, విద్యార్థి, మహాత్ముడు, పద్మనాభుడు are Sanskrit compounds. Analyse the ones you already know before learning new ones.
**Use Telugu names.** Every friend called శ్రీనివాస్, హృషీకేశ్ or జనార్దన్ is a Sahasranāma name and a compound type (lesson 13.8).

**Watch for false friends.** Telugu meanings sometimes drift: Telugu "సంసారం" means family life, but Sanskrit संसार is the cycle of births; Telugu "ఉపన్యాసం" is a speech, Sanskrit उपन्यास is a statement or proposal.

blocks.text: Learn these lines by heart. Each one is a complete, memorable example of one rule. When you forget a rule, recite its anchor and the rule comes back with it.

blocks.title: Build your own anchors
text: When you learn a new rule from a verse you love, add a line to this table in a notebook. The best anchor is a line you already chant: from the Sahasranāma, the Suprabhātam, or a stotra your family recites.

blocks.text: A memory palace for the cases
If you like visual memory, put the eight cases in the rooms of a house you know well (your childhood home in Andhra or Telangana works perfectly):

head: Room
Case

lessons.title: సారాంశ పట్టికలు · Cheat sheets
lessons.summary: The whole grammar on a few pages: noun endings for the main stems, the personal pronouns and तद्, verb endings for all ten lakāras, participles, sandhi, compounds, kṛt and taddhita suffixes, kārakas and the words that demand a case, an ending finder for reading, and the Telugu-only and Sanskrit-only lists. Use these for revision after the lessons, not instead of them.

blocks.text: Each sheet collects a part of the grammar you have already met. The lesson number in each heading takes you back to the full explanation, examples and exceptions.

blocks.title: Cover and recite
text: Cover one column with a card and say the forms aloud, top to bottom. Then cover a row and say it across. When you can do both without looking, move to the next sheet. Ten minutes on one sheet a day goes through all of them in two weeks.

blocks.title: No flash cards here
text: These tables are not turned into flash cards: every row already has a card in its own lesson.

blocks.title: Three forms for the dual
text: Every noun has only three dual forms: one for 1st/2nd/vocative, one ending -भ्याम् for 3rd/4th/5th, one ending -ओः for 6th/7th. Learn the dual of a stem in one breath: रामौ रामाभ्याम् रामयोः.

blocks.title: What never changes
text: Look down the plural columns: -भिः, -भ्यः, -नाम्/-णाम् and -सु/-षु are the same for every stem except राम and वन (रामैः, रामेभ्यः). Learn those four endings once and you know a third of every plural table.

blocks.title: Neuter is masculine with three changes
text: वन is declined exactly like राम except in the 1st and 2nd cases (and vocative): वनम्, वने, वनानि. The other a-stem neuters work the same way. Neuter i- and u-stems (वारि, मधु) also add न् before vowel endings: वारिणे, मधुनः.

blocks.text: The Telugu case list and Sanskrit (lesson 2.3)

blocks.title: Same names, different jobs
text: Telugu borrowed the eight names from Sanskrit, but the jobs differ at the edges. Telugu "రామునికి ఇచ్చాడు" uses షష్ఠీ కి for "to", where Sanskrit uses the 4th case (रामाय ददाति). Telugu "ఇంటిలో" is షష్ఠీ లో, where Sanskrit uses the 7th (गृहे). Trust the Sanskrit case, not the Telugu label.

blocks.title: The short forms in brackets
text: मे, ते, नः, वः, नौ, वाम्, मा, त्वा never begin a sentence or a verse quarter. You know them from prayers: "मे" in "कुरु मे देव", "नः" in "शं नो मित्रः", "ते" in "नमस्ते".

blocks.title: No gender in "I" and "you"
text: अस्मद् and युष्मद् are the same for men, women and things, just like నేను and నువ్వు. Gender begins with "he, she, it" (तद्).

blocks.text: The neuter is तत् ते तानि in the 1st and 2nd cases and the same as the masculine everywhere else. एतद् "this" is तद् with ए- in front (एषः, एषा, एतत्), and यद् "who, which" follows the same pattern (यः, या, यत्). सर्व "all" uses the pronoun endings -स्मै, -स्मात्, -स्मिन्, -षाम् but is otherwise like राम.

blocks.title: सर्वनाम endings
text: Pronouns differ from राम in five places: -स्मै (not -आय), -स्मात् (not -आत्), -स्मिन् (not -ए) and -ते, -एषाम् in the plural (not -आः, -आणाम्). "स्मै स्मात् स्मिन्": the pronoun signature. You hear it in "तस्मै श्रीगुरवे नमः".

blocks.text: Verb endings: the present system of भू, परस्मैपद (lessons 6.3, 6.4, 6.6)

blocks.title: ప్రథమ పురుష is "he", not "I"
text: Sanskrit grammar counts persons from the other end. प्रथम पुरुष is the 3rd person (he, she, it), मध्यम पुरुष is "you", and उत्तम पुरुष is "I, we". Telugu school grammar follows the same Sanskrit names, so this should already feel familiar.

blocks.title: परस्मैपद "i", आत्मनेपद "e"
text: In the present, परस्मैपद endings end in -इ (ति, सि, मि, न्ति) and आत्मनेपद endings end in -ए (ते, से, ए, न्ते). "भवति, लभते": i for the other, e for oneself.

blocks.text: All ten lakāras at a glance (lessons 6.3–6.6)

blocks.title: The names are a code
text: The ten names are ल + a vowel + ट् or ङ्: लट् लिट् लुट् लृट् लेट् लोट् and लङ् लिङ् लुङ् लृङ्. (लेट् is the Vedic subjunctive and is not used in Classical Sanskrit, which is why there are ten and not eleven.) The three ङ् lakāras that are pasts, लङ् लुङ् लृङ्, are exactly the ones that take the augment अ- (अभवत्, अभूत्, अभविष्यत्), by Pāṇini 6.4.71. "ङ् and past: put अ in front."

blocks.title: Find the future by its स्य
text: Any verb with -स्य- or -ष्य- before the ending is future (लृट्) or conditional (लृङ्): भविष्यति, करिष्यति, लप्स्यते, दास्यति. If it also has the augment अ- in front, it is the conditional: अभविष्यत्.

blocks.title: One stem, three forms
text: The past participle, the absolutive and the infinitive usually share one stem: कृ-त, कृ-त्वा, कर्-तुम्; दृष्-ट, दृष्-ट्वा, द्रष्-टुम्. Learn the -त form first: -त्वा almost always follows it, and -तुम् usually has the same consonant, with a strengthened vowel.

blocks.title: Telugu has every one of these
text: చేయబడిన (कृत), చేస్తున్న (कुर्वत्), చేసి (कृत्वा), చేయడానికి (कर्तुम्), చేయదగిన/చేయవలసిన (कर्तव्य). The Telugu forms are your translation key: "చేసి" in Telugu is always क्त्वा or ल्यप् in Sanskrit.

blocks.title: Two questions settle visarga
text: First: what vowel is before the ः? Then: what sound comes after it? अः + soft becomes ओ; आः + soft just loses the ः; any other vowel + soft gives र्. Before a hard consonant, the ः turns into the sibilant of that consonant's row (श् for च, ष् for ट, स् for त) or stays.

ఉదాహరణ
rows: final stop becomes voiced before a vowel or voiced consonant
जगत् + ईशः → जगदीशः, वाक् + ईशः → वागीशः
final stop becomes nasal before a nasal
जगत् + नाथः → जगन्नाथः, वाक् + मयम् → वाङ्मयम्

blocks.title: Sounds move toward their neighbour
text: Almost every consonant sandhi makes the first sound more like the second: voiced before voiced, nasal before nasal, palatal before palatal (त् + च → च्च), ल before ल. Say the two words fast and your mouth does the sandhi for you.

గుర్తు

blocks.title: Four questions in order
text: Is the whole an adverb? अव्ययीभाव. Does it mean "X and Y"? द्वन्द्व. Does it describe someone not named in it? बहुव्रीहि. Otherwise it is a तत्पुरुष (with कर्मधारय and द्विगु as its kinds). Ask in this order and you will rarely be wrong.

blocks.title: vṛddhi says "of"
text: When the first vowel of a familiar name has grown (अ → आ, इ → ऐ, उ → औ) and the word has a suffix, read it as "son of, follower of, belonging to": वासुदेव, शैव, वैष्णव, कौन्तेय, पार्थ (पृथा's son). The Gītā calls Arjuna by a dozen of these.

blocks.title: Six roles, one sentence
text: "In the garden (अधिकरण), Rāma (कर्ता) plucks with his hand (करण) a flower (कर्म) from the tree (अपादान) for Sītā (सम्प्रदान)": उद्याने रामः हस्तेन वृक्षात् सीतायै पुष्पं चिनोति. One sentence that holds all six roles. Say it daily for a week.

blocks.title: These are Telugu postpositions
text: सह is "తో", विना is "లేకుండా", प्रति is "వైపు", परितः is "చుట్టూ". Telugu puts the postposition after the noun; Sanskrit does the same with these words, but also changes the noun's case.

blocks.text: Ending finder: what is this word? (for reading)
When you meet an unknown word in a verse, look at its end. This table lists the commonest endings and what they usually are.

head: ముగింపు
సాధారణంగా
ఉదాహరణ

अ- before the root, past ending (-त्, -न्, -त, -न्त)
iast: verb, present, he / they (Ā); or 7th sing. of a -ta noun
a- before the root, past ending (-t, -n, -ta, -nta)

blocks.title: Read words from the right
text: Telugu speakers already read from the right: in రాముని యొక్క the meaning sits in the ending. Sanskrit is the same, only more so. Train your eye to jump to the last two syllables of a word before reading the start.

blocks.text: What Telugu has that Sanskrit lacks (lesson 2.6)

items: Gender in the verb: చేశాడు, చేసింది. Sanskrit verbs show person and number only: अकरोत् for both.
Inclusive and exclusive "we": మనం and మేము. Sanskrit has only वयम्.
A whole negative conjugation: చేయను, చేయడు. Sanskrit adds न to the positive verb.
Human versus non-human in the plural: వాళ్ళు versus అవి. Sanskrit uses grammatical gender.
Telugu-only sandhis: ఆమ్రేడిత, గసడదవాదేశ, ద్రుతప్రకృతికం, త్రిక సంధి and others.
The ద్రుతం (the final న్ of Telugu words that comes and goes).
Postpositions instead of case endings, and a single plural ending -లు.
Verb-final word order, which is fixed; Sanskrit word order is free.

blocks.text: What Sanskrit has that Telugu lacks (lesson 2.7)

items: The dual number: रामौ, भवतः.
Three genders that do not follow meaning: दाराः "wife" is masculine plural.
Adjectives that agree with the noun in gender, number and case.
Many noun classes, each with its own endings.
Ten lakāras and two sets of endings, परस्मैपद and आत्मनेपद.
Ten verb classes (gaṇas), 22 verb prefixes and derived verbs (causative, desiderative, intensive, denominative).
Obligatory sandhi between words, inside sentences.
Long compounds and the absolute constructions (सति सप्तमी).
Free word order, because the endings carry the meaning.

blocks.title: Pack light, then pack heavy
text: Before reading Sanskrit, put down the Telugu-only items (gender in the verb, మనం/మేము, negative verbs). Then pick up the Sanskrit-only items one at a time, in the order of the lessons.

quiz.q: Which form is the 4th case singular of गुरु?
quiz.why: गुरु takes guṇa before the 4th-case ending: गुरु → गुरो → गुरव् + ए = गुरवे. गुरोः is 5th/6th and गुरौ is 7th.

quiz.q: In Telugu "రాముడు అడవికి వెళ్ళాడు", అడవికి uses షష్ఠీ కి. What case does Sanskrit use for "to the forest"?
quiz.why: The destination of a verb of motion is its कर्म, so it takes the 2nd case: वनं गच्छति. The Telugu case label is not a guide here.
-ष्य- makes it a future-system form, and the augment अ- in front makes it the conditional, लृङ्.

quiz.q: तद्धितम् comes from तत् + हितम्. Which rule applies?
options: म् before a consonant becomes anusvāra
quiz.why: Final त् becomes द् before a voiced sound, and the following ह takes on the voiced aspiration of द: द्ध.

quiz.q: पीताम्बरः "the one whose garment is yellow" is which compound?
quiz.why: It describes someone (Kṛṣṇa) who is not named in the compound: पीतम् अम्बरं यस्य सः. पीतम् अम्बरम् alone, "the yellow garment", would be a कर्मधारय.

quiz.q: What does प्रणम्य tell you, before you even know the root?
quiz.why: A word starting with a prefix (प्र-) and ending in -य is usually ल्यप्, the absolutive used with prefixes: प्रणम्य "having bowed".

lessons.title: అధ్యయన ప్రణాళిక · A study plan, and what comes next
lessons.summary: A twelve-month plan through this course with daily routines of 15, 30 and 60 minutes and a milestone for each month; what to read after the course, in order of difficulty; the reference books to own; and an honest account of what "all the rules" in this course does and does not cover.

blocks.text: The plan assumes 30 minutes a day, six days a week. With 15 minutes, take two years; with an hour, nine months. The order is the order of the lessons: each unit uses the ones before it.

blocks.title: One milestone a month
text: Write the twelve milestones on a card and tick them off. A month that ends without its milestone is not a failure: repeat it. Slow and complete beats fast and patchy, because every unit is built on the one before.

head: సమయం
రోజువారీ పని
rows: 5 min: flash cards due today. 7 min: one section of the current lesson, read aloud. 3 min: recite one table or verse from memory.
10 min: flash cards due today. 15 min: the current lesson, with its worked examples and quiz. 5 min: recite your anchor verses (lesson 14.1).
15 min: flash cards. 25 min: the current lesson. 10 min: one verse from unit 13, split and parsed in a notebook. 10 min: chant a table or a stotra aloud.

blocks.title: Never skip the cards
text: If you have only five minutes, spend them on the cards due today. The lessons can wait a day; the spacing of the reviews cannot.

blocks.text: Once a week, take a day off from new material: redo the quizzes of the last three lessons, and recite everything you have memorised. On that day also write out one verse from memory with its anvaya and word meanings.

items: **Read aloud.** Sanskrit was made to be heard. Every table, rule and verse goes in faster through the ear and mouth than through the eye.
**Keep a notebook.** For each verse you study: the verse, the split, the anvaya, each word with its form (e.g. "रामाय: राम, m, 4th sing."), and the meaning in Telugu.
**Parse everything.** For every word you read, ask: noun or verb? Which case, number, gender, or which person, number, lakāra? Once this is a habit, reading becomes easy.
**Use your Telugu.** When a word looks familiar, check the Telugu meaning against the Sanskrit one (lesson 14.1 lists the false friends).
**Recite with a group.** If there is a Gītā or Sahasranāma group near you, join it. Group chanting is the pāṭhaśālā method, and it works.

blocks.title: Online tools
text: The Gita Supersite of IIT Kanpur has the Gītā with several commentaries and translations. sanskritdocuments.org has stotras in many scripts, including Telugu. The Sanskrit Heritage site (Gérard Huet) can split sandhi and parse words automatically: use it to check your own parsing, not to replace it.

blocks.title: Speaking
text: Saṃskṛta Bhāratī runs short spoken-Sanskrit camps (सम्भाषण शिबिर) in many cities and online. Ten days of speaking does more for fluency than months of reading.

blocks.text: What "all the rules" covers in this course
This course sets out to teach the whole grammar of Classical Sanskrit, the language of the Gītā, the purāṇas, the stotras and kāvya. It covers:

items: the script and every sound, with the Telugu–Devanagari mapping;
every major noun class and the irregular nouns, all pronouns and numbers;
all ten lakāras, both padas, the ten gaṇas, passives, the four derived verbs and the 22 prefixes;
all participles, absolutives, infinitives and gerundives, and the main kṛt and taddhita suffixes;
all vowel, consonant and visarga sandhi rules you will meet in texts;
every type of compound and how to unpack long ones;
the kārakas, the words that govern cases, absolute constructions and anvaya;
the main metres of the Gītā and the stotras.

prompt.head: జ్ఞాపకం · memory aid
prompt.text: -డు is రామః, -స్సు is मनः, -త్తు is जगत्
prompt.iast: -డు is రామః, -స్సు is manaḥ, -త్తు is jagat

answer.text: The Telugu ending tells you the Sanskrit class. -డు → masculine అ-stem (రాముడు → रामः). -స్సు → s-stem neuter (మనస్సు → मनः). -త్తు → t-stem (జగత్తు → जगत्). -మంతుడు/-వంతుడు → -मत्/-वत् (బుద్ధిమంతుడు → बुद्धिमान्). Telugu doubled the final consonant and added ఉ because a Telugu word cannot end in a consonant.
answer.iast: The Telugu ending tells you the Sanskrit class. -డు → masculine అ-stem (రాముడు → rāmaḥ). -స్సు → s-stem neuter (మనస్సు → manaḥ). -త్తు → t-stem (జగత్తు → jagat). -మంతుడు/-వంతుడు → -mat/-vat (బుద్ధిమంతుడు → buddhimān). Telugu doubled the final consonant and added ఉ because a Telugu word cannot end in a consonant.

answer.text: కర్మ చేయడంలో మాత్రమే నీకు అధికారం ఉంది, దాని ఫలాలపై ఎప్పుడూ లేదు. కర్మఫలానికి కారణం నువ్వే అనుకోకు. కర్మ చేయకుండా ఉండటంపై కూడా ఆసక్తి పెట్టుకోకు.

answer.head: తెలుగు భావం
answer.text: రాముడు రావణుని చంపుతున్నాడు (మూడు వాక్యాలకూ ఒకే అర్థం).

answer.head: ప్రతిపదార్థం · word by word
answer.text: रामः = రాముడు (కర్త, ప్రథమా); रावणम् = రావణుని (కర్మ, ద్వితీయా); हन्ति = చంపుతున్నాడు (వర్తమానం)
answer.iast: rāmaḥ = రాముడు (కర్త, ప్రథమా); rāvaṇam = రావణుని (కర్మ, ద్వితీయా); hanti = చంపుతున్నాడు (వర్తమానం)

answer.head: వ్యాకరణం · grammar
answer.text: The endings -ः (subject) and -म् (object) do the work that word order does in English. Swap them, रामं रावणः हन्ति, and the meaning reverses.
answer.iast: The endings -ḥ (subject) and -m (object) do the work that word order does in English. Swap them, rāmaṃ rāvaṇaḥ hanti, and the meaning reverses.

prompt.text: Three questions for a new noun

answer.text: (1) What is the stem? (2) What is the gender? (3) What is the nominative singular? Learn धर्मः (m.), not "dharma"; ज्ञानम् (n.), not "jñāna"; मतिः (f.), not "mati". The nominative + gender tells you which table to use.
answer.iast: (1) What is the stem? (2) What is the gender? (3) What is the nominative singular? Learn dharmaḥ (m.), not "dharma"; jñānam (n.), not "jñāna"; matiḥ (f.), not "mati". The nominative + gender tells you which table to use.

answer.text: Whenever there are exactly two — two eyes, two hands, Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa — Sanskrit uses the dual, and the verb is dual too: रामलक्ष्मणौ वनं गच्छतः. The dual endings are few (three per noun class, three per verb tense), so learn them as a set.
answer.iast: Whenever there are exactly two — two eyes, two hands, Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa — Sanskrit uses the dual, and the verb is dual too: rāmalakṣmaṇau vanaṃ gacchataḥ. The dual endings are few (three per noun class, three per verb tense), so learn them as a set.

answer.iast: Chant the Telugu list as you learnt it — డుముపులు ప్రథమ, నిన్ నున్ లన్ గూర్చి గుఱించి ద్వితీయ, చేతన్ చేన్ తోడన్ తోన్ తృతీయ, కొఱకున్ కై చతుర్థి, వలనన్ కంటెన్ పట్టి పంచమి, కిన్ కున్ యొక్క లోన్ లోపలన్ షష్ఠి, అందున్ నన్ సప్తమి, ఓ ఓరి ఓయి ఓసి సంబోధన — and after each line say the Sanskrit form: rāmaḥ, rāmam, rāmeṇa, rāmāya, rāmāt, rāmasya, rāme, he rāma.

prompt.iast: paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṃ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām | / dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya saṃbhavāmi yuge yuge ||

answer.head: తెలుగు భావం
answer.text: సజ్జనులను రక్షించడానికి, దుష్టులను నాశనం చేయడానికి, ధర్మాన్ని స్థాపించడానికి నేను ప్రతి యుగంలోనూ అవతరిస్తాను.

answer.text: For the protection of the pious, the destruction of the evil-doers, and the establishment of virtue, I manifest myself in every age.

answer.head: వ్యాకరణం · grammar

answer.iast: paritrāṇāya, vināśāya, dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya: three datives of purpose (చతుర్థీ, Telugu -కొఱకు, -కై).

answer.text: साधूनाम्, दुष्कृताम्: genitive plurals: "of the good", "of the evildoers".
answer.iast: sādhūnām, duṣkṛtām: genitive plurals: "of the good", "of the evildoers".

answer.iast: yuge yuge: locative of time, repeated: "in age after age", Telugu యుగయుగమునందు.

cards.id: verbs:कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । / मा कर्मफल
cards.context: Two things Sanskrit verbs have that Telugu verbs don't

prompt.head: Gītā 2.47
prompt.text: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । / मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
prompt.iast: karmaṇyevādhikāraste mā phaleṣu kadācana | / mā karmaphalaheturbhūrmā te saṅgo'stvakarmaṇi ||

answer.head: పదచ్ఛేదం · word split
answer.text: कर्मणि एव अधिकारः ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुः भूः मा ते सङ्गः अस्तु अकर्मणि ॥
answer.iast: karmaṇi eva adhikāraḥ te mā phaleṣu kadācana | mā karmaphalahetuḥ bhūḥ mā te saṅgaḥ astu akarmaṇi ||

answer.head: తెలుగు భావం
answer.text: కర్మ చేయడంలో మాత్రమే నీకు అధికారం ఉంది, దాని ఫలాలపై ఎప్పుడూ లేదు. కర్మఫలానికి కారణం నువ్వే అనుకోకు. కర్మ చేయకుండా ఉండటంపై కూడా ఆసక్తి పెట్టుకోకు.

answer.head: English
answer.text: Your right is only to act, not to the results. Do not be the cause of the results of action. Do not have any inclination towards inaction.

answer.head: ప్రతిపదార్థం · word by word
answer.text: कर्मणि = కర్మయందు; एव = మాత్రమే; अधिकारः = అధికారం; ते = నీకు; मा = వద్దు; फलेषु = ఫలాలయందు; कदाचन = ఎప్పుడూ; कर्मफलहेतुः = కర్మఫలానికి కారణం; भूः = అవ్వకు (मा + लुङ्); सङ्गः = ఆసక్తి; अस्तु = ఉండుగాక (लोट्); अकर्मणि = కర్మ చేయకపోవడంలో
answer.iast: karmaṇi = కర్మయందు; eva = మాత్రమే; adhikāraḥ = అధికారం; te = నీకు; mā = వద్దు; phaleṣu = ఫలాలయందు; kadācana = ఎప్పుడూ; karmaphalahetuḥ = కర్మఫలానికి కారణం; bhūḥ = అవ్వకు (mā + luṅ); saṅgaḥ = ఆసక్తి; astu = ఉండుగాక (loṭ); akarmaṇi = కర్మ చేయకపోవడంలో

answer.head: వ్యాకరణం · grammar
answer.text: मा भूः "do not be" is the classical prohibitive: मा + aorist (लुङ्) without the augment अ: अभूः → भूः. Telugu నిషేధార్థకం: కాకుము.
answer.iast: mā bhūḥ "do not be" is the classical prohibitive: mā + aorist (luṅ) without the augment a: abhūḥ → bhūḥ. Telugu నిషేధార్థకం: కాకుము.

answer.head: వ్యాకరణం · grammar
answer.text: अस्तु "let it be" is लोट् (command / wish), 3rd person: Telugu ఉండుగాక.
answer.iast: astu "let it be" is loṭ (command / wish), 3rd person: Telugu ఉండుగాక.

answer.head: వ్యాకరణం · grammar
answer.text: ते is the short form of तव / तुभ्यम् "your / to you". Telugu నీకు.
answer.iast: te is the short form of tava / tubhyam "your / to you". Telugu నీకు.

cards.id: sentences:క-words ask, య-words relate, త-words point

prompt.head: జ్ఞాపకం · memory aid
prompt.text: క-words ask, య-words relate, త-words point

answer.text: కః (who?), యః (who, the one that), సః (he). కదా (when?), యదా (when, as in "when X…"), తదా (then). కుత్ర (where?), యత్ర (where…), తత్ర (there). One pattern, dozens of words. Gītā 18.78: यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णः … तत्र श्रीः "where Kṛṣṇa is … there is fortune".
answer.iast: కః (who?), యః (who, the one that), సః (he). కదా (when?), యదా (when, as in "when X…"), తదా (then). కుత్ర (where?), యత్ర (where…), తత్ర (there). One pattern, dozens of words. Gītā 18.78: yatra yogeśvaraḥ kṛṣṇaḥ … tatra śrīḥ "where Kṛṣṇa is … there is fortune".

prompt.head: Gītā 3.21
prompt.text: यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः । / स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते ॥
prompt.iast: yadyadācarati śreṣṭhastattadevetaro janaḥ | / sa yatpramāṇaṃ kurute lokastadanuvartate ||

answer.head: తెలుగు భావం
answer.text: శ్రేష్ఠుడు ఏది చేస్తాడో ఇతరులు కూడా అదే చేస్తారు. అతను దేనిని ప్రమాణంగా నిలబెడతాడో లోకం దానినే అనుసరిస్తుంది.

answer.head: English
answer.text: Whatever a superior person does, another person does the same! Whatever they uphold as authority, an ordinary person follows that.

answer.head: వ్యాకరణం · grammar
answer.text: यद्यत् … तत्तत्: "whatever … that very thing": the relative pronoun doubled for "whatever".
answer.iast: yadyat … tattat: "whatever … that very thing": the relative pronoun doubled for "whatever".

answer.head: వ్యాకరణం · grammar
answer.text: सः यत् प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकः तत् अनुवर्तते: "what standard he sets, that the world follows": a यत् … तत् pair.
answer.iast: saḥ yat pramāṇaṃ kurute lokaḥ tat anuvartate: "what standard he sets, that the world follows": a yat … tat pair.

answer.head: వ్యాకరణం · grammar
answer.text: Telugu builds the same thought with a participle: శ్రేష్ఠుడు ఏది ఆచరిస్తాడో, దానినే ఇతరులూ ఆచరిస్తారు — Telugu too uses ఏది…అదే, a borrowed relative pattern.

cards.id: sentences:Passive = agent in తృతీయా, object in ప్రథమా

prompt.head: జ్ఞాపకం · memory aid

cards.id: sentences:अहं गीतां पठामि इति माता जानाति । किं त्वम् अपि

prompt.head: సంస్కృతం
prompt.text: अहं गीतां पठामि इति माता जानाति । किं त्वम् अपि पठसि ?
prompt.iast: ahaṃ gītāṃ paṭhāmi iti mātā jānāti | kiṃ tvam api paṭhasi ?

answer.head: తెలుగు భావం
answer.text: నేను గీత చదువుతున్నానని అమ్మకు తెలుసు. నువ్వు కూడా చదువుతున్నావా?

answer.head: English
answer.text: Mother knows that I am reading the Gītā. Are you reading it too?

answer.head: ప్రతిపదార్థం · word by word
answer.text: अहम् = నేను; गीताम् = గీతను; पठामि = చదువుతున్నాను; इति = అని; माता = అమ్మ; जानाति = ఎరుగును; किम् = ఆ? (question); त्वम् = నువ్వు; अपि = కూడా; पठसि = చదువుతున్నావు
answer.iast: aham = నేను; gītām = గీతను; paṭhāmi = చదువుతున్నాను; iti = అని; mātā = అమ్మ; jānāti = ఎరుగును; kim = ఆ? (question); tvam = నువ్వు; api = కూడా; paṭhasi = చదువుతున్నావు

answer.head: వ్యాకరణం · grammar
answer.text: इति closes the quoted thought, as అని does.
answer.iast: iti closes the quoted thought, as అని does.

answer.head: వ్యాకరణం · grammar
answer.text: "అమ్మకు తెలుసు" becomes माता जानाति: the knower is the subject in Sanskrit.
answer.iast: "అమ్మకు తెలుసు" becomes mātā jānāti: the knower is the subject in Sanskrit.

answer.head: English
answer.text: We are going. We two are going.

answer.head: ప్రతిపదార్థం · word by word

answer.iast: vayam = మేము or మనము; gacchāmaḥ = వెళ్తున్నాము (ఉత్తమ బహు.); āvām = మేమిద్దరం / మనమిద్దరం; gacchāvaḥ = ఇద్దరం వెళ్తున్నాము (ఉత్తమ ద్వి.)

answer.head: వ్యాకరణం · grammar
answer.text: Sanskrit does not distinguish inclusive and exclusive "we". It distinguishes "we two" from "we (three or more)".
